A-AC-DhU-system-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal account creation activity for system user: {user|featureValue|histogram}

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation')=1

A-AC-DhU-system-A.ClassifyIf: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation')=1
A-AC-DhU-system-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal account creation activity for system user {user|featureValue|histogram} on this asset
A-AC-DhU-system-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for account creation activity by system account on this asset. Account creation events are notable because they can provide a path for an attacker to move laterally through a system.
A-AC-DhU-system-A.RuleName: Abnormal account creation by system account on asset

A-AC-DhU-system-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First account creation activity for system user: {user|featureValue|histogram}

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation')=1

A-AC-DhU-system-F.ClassifyIf: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation')=1
A-AC-DhU-system-F.ReasonTemplate: First account creation activity for user {user|featureValue|histogram} on this asset
A-AC-DhU-system-F.RuleDescription: First time a system user performs account creation activity on the asset. This can be indicative of malicious activity
A-AC-DhU-system-F.RuleName: First account creation by system account on asset

A-ACCT-CR-DEL.ReasonTemplate: Account {user|event.account_name} was created and deleted on this asset in the same sequence.
A-ACCT-CR-DEL.RuleDescription: An account was created and deleted on the asset. This could indicate an attacker covering their tracks
A-ACCT-CR-DEL.RuleName: Account created and deleted on asset

A-AD-Diagnostic-Tool.AggregateReasonTemplate: Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe) invoked on this asset
A-AD-Diagnostic-Tool.ReasonTemplate: Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe) invoked on this asset
A-AD-Diagnostic-Tool.RuleDescription: The ntdsutil.exe was run on this asset, which can be used for various attacks against the NTDS database (NTDS.DIT). This is an indicator of potentially malicious activity, therefore this event is notable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_ntdsutil.yml
A-AD-Diagnostic-Tool.RuleName: Invocation of Active Directory Diagnostic Tool (ntdsutil.exe) on this asset

A-AE-SwSh-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First NTLM authentication by {default|featureValue|histogram} in the organization
A-AE-SwSh-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for host {default|featureValue|histogram} to use NTLM authentication in the organization.
A-AE-SwSh-F.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected a host using NTLM for the first time. In most cases this is benign but could also indicate a pass the hash attempt.
A-AE-SwSh-F.RuleName: New server hostname using NTLM authentication in the organization.

A-AL-DhU-A.ReasonTemplate: Unusual for user {user|featureValue|histogram} to log into this asset
A-AL-DhU-A.RuleDescription: Unusual logon for the user to the asset

A-AL-DhU-F.ReasonTemplate: First time user {user|featureValue|histogram} has logged into this asset
A-AL-DhU-F.RuleDescription: First time this user has logged into the asset

A-AL-DhU-count.RuleDescription: Abnormal number of users have logged into this asset

A-ALERT.RuleDescription: A security alert is associated with the asset.

A-ALERT-COMPROMISED-POWERSHELL.ReasonTemplate: Security alert and powershell detected on a host
A-ALERT-COMPROMISED-POWERSHELL.RuleDescription: Security alerts were detected on a host that powershell was run on. This is noteworthy because powershell is a powerful tool that could be exploited for hacking. If it was detected on a host which had a security alert it may mean the host is compromised.

A-ALERT-Critical.AggregateReasonTemplate: Security Alert on Critical System asset by this user: {default|featureValue}
A-ALERT-Critical.RuleDescription: An entity/device/user has accessed an Critical Asset and has also triggered a security-alert
A-ALERT-Critical.RuleName: Security Alert on a critical asset

A-ALERT-DISTINCT-NAMES.ReasonTemplate: Third distinct security alert on asset
A-ALERT-DISTINCT-NAMES.RuleDescription: At least three distinct security alerts were reported for the asset. This raises the probability that the asset is compromised.

A-ALERT-DL.AggregateReasonTemplate: Exabeam DL correlation rule alert on {asset|event.local_asset|info}
A-ALERT-DL.RuleDescription: Exabeam DL has raised a Security Alert on this asset.
A-ALERT-DL.RuleExpression: CountByIf(local_asset_alert_name, org, add_risk_to_asset='true' && session_label!='vpn-in' && vendor='Exabeam DL','security-alert')=1
A-ALERT-DL.RuleName: DL Correlation rule alert on asset

A-ALERT-Log4j.AggregateReasonTemplate: Alert associated with Log4j vulnerability detected on asset : {default|featureValue}
A-ALERT-Log4j.RuleDescription: An alert associated with known Log4j Vulnerability has triggered from a third party vendor. This is notable as this vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker to control log messages and execute malicious code.
A-ALERT-Log4j.RuleName: Alert associated with an exploitation or post exploitation as seen with Log4j Vulnerability was detected.

A-ALERT-Other.RuleDescription: A network or similar alert is associated with the asset.

A-AM-DhU-system-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First account management activity for system user: {user|featureValue|histogram}

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation', 'member-added')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-NEW-ASSET')

A-AM-DhU-system-F.ClassifyIf: countByIf(user, dest_host, (EndsWith(user, '$') || InList(user, 'system', 'anonymous logon', 'network service', 'local service')), 'account-creation','member-added')=1
A-AM-DhU-system-F.ReasonTemplate: First account management activity for user {user|featureValue|histogram} on this asset
A-AM-DhU-system-F.RuleDescription: First time a system user performs account management activity on the asset. This can be indicative of malicious activity
A-AM-DhU-system-F.RuleName: First account management by system account on asset

A-APP-Log4j-String.AggregateReasonTemplate: App activity containing keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on this asset: jndi:{default|featureValue}
A-APP-Log4j-String.ReasonTemplate: App activity containing keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on this asset: jndi:{default|featureValue}
A-APP-Log4j-String.RuleDescription: App activity containing keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on this asset. This is notable as this vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker to control log messages and execute arbitrary code.
A-APP-Log4j-String.RuleName: There was an attempt via app activity to exploit the CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability on this asset.

A-APT-Hurricane-Panda.AggregateReasonTemplate: Artifacts from APT group 'Hurricane Panda' observed
A-APT-Hurricane-Panda.ReasonTemplate: Artifacts from APT group 'Hurricane Panda' observed
A-APT-Hurricane-Panda.RuleDescription: Artifacts used by the APT group 'Hurricane Panda' have been observed. APT related activity warrants a closer inspection. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_hurricane_panda.yml
A-APT-Hurricane-Panda.RuleName: Artifacts used by the APT group 'Hurricane Panda' have been observed on this asset

A-ATP-PSexec.AggregateReasonTemplate: PSExec service was run on the asset.
A-ATP-PSexec.ReasonTemplate: PSExec service was run on the asset.
A-ATP-PSexec.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted psexec service was run on the host which is used to run something on a remote server folder. This is notable as this is a known method of the HAFNIUM actor responsible for the Microsoft Exchange vulnerability exploits.
A-ATP-PSexec.RuleName: PSExec service was run on the asset.

A-ATP-Tool-FGDump.AggregateReasonTemplate: Malicious process/file was run from a temp folder: {default|featureValue}
A-ATP-Tool-FGDump.ReasonTemplate: Sensitive process/file {default|event.file_name} was run from a temp folder
A-ATP-Tool-FGDump.RuleDescription: A malicious exe/dll known for credential dumping was run from a temp folder. This is notable as it is a part of a fgdump credential dumping tool which can be used to get login information for lateral movement activities.

A-ATP-Tool-PSTGDump.AggregateReasonTemplate: Malicious process/file was run from a temp folder: {default|featureValue} on this asset.
A-ATP-Tool-PSTGDump.ReasonTemplate: Sensitive process/file {default|event.file_name} was run from a temp folderi on this asset.
A-ATP-Tool-PSTGDump.RuleDescription: A malicious mstgdump.exe was run from a temp folder. This is notable as it is a part of the pstgdump credential dumping toolwhich can be used to get login information for lateral movement activities.
A-ATP-Tool-PSTGDump.RuleName: Malicious pstgdump.exe was run from a temp folder on this asset.

A-AccountDiscovery.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, ((((InList(toLower(process_name), 'whoami.exe', 'quser.exe', 'qwinsta.exe')) || (toLower(process_name)='wmic.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), 'useraccount') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'get')) || (toLower(process_name)='cmdkey.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), '/list')) or (toLower(process_name)='cmd.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), '/c') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'dir ') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\users\\'))) && !contains(toLower(command_line), ' rmdir ')) || (InList(toLower(process_name), 'net.exe', 'net1.exe') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'user') && !containsany(toLower(command_line), '/domain', '/add', '/delete', '/active', '/expires', '/passwordreq', '/scriptpath', '/times', '/workstations'))), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-AccountDiscovery')
A-AccountDiscovery.RuleName: Local accounts were enumerated on this asset

A-App-Log4j-String-2.AggregateReasonTemplate: App activity containing known keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on the asset.
A-App-Log4j-String-2.ReasonTemplate: App activity containing known keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on the asset.
A-App-Log4j-String-2.RuleDescription: App activity containing known keywords related to CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability was detected on the asset. This is notable as this vulnerability can be exploited by an attacker to control log messages and execute arbitrary code.

A-Applocker-Bypass.AggregateReasonTemplate: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker on this asset.
A-Applocker-Bypass.ReasonTemplate: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker on this asset.
A-Applocker-Bypass.RuleDescription: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker whitelisting was performed on this asset. This method is a way to execute arbitrary code in an Applocker whitelisting environment. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_possible_applocker_bypass.yml
A-Applocker-Bypass.RuleName: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker on this asset

A-Archer.ReasonTemplate: Known malware, 'Archer', has been executed by the 'rundll32' executable
A-Archer.RuleDescription: Known malware, 'Archer', has been executed by the 'rundll32' executable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_crime_fireball.yml

A-AutoRun-Modification.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, toLower(process_name)='reg.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), 'add') && containsany(toLower(command_line), '\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run','\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonce','\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonceex','\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runservices','\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runservicesonce','\\software\\microsoft\\windows ,t\\currentversion\\winlogon\\userinit','\\software\\microsoft\\windows nt\\currentversion\\winlogon\\shell','\\software\\microsoft\\windows nt\\currentversion\\windows','\\software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\explorer\\user shell folders','\\system\\currentcontrolset\\control\\safeboot\\alternateshell'), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-AutoRun-Modification')
A-AutoRun-Modification.RuleName: AutoRun Keys modified using reg.exe on this asset

A-BITS-Suspicious-Service.AggregateReasonTemplate: First abnormal BITS job created on this asset using process: {default|event.process_name}
A-BITS-Suspicious-Service.ReasonTemplate: First abnormal BITS job created on this asset using process: {default|event.process_name}
A-BITS-Suspicious-Service.RuleDescription: A BITS job was created on the asset to transfer/create an unknown file from an unknown server. This is notable as BITS jobs can be used to maintain persistence or evade detection by removing malicious payloads.
A-BITS-Suspicious-Service.RuleName: First abnormal BITS job created on the asset.

A-Baby-Shark-Activity.AggregateReasonTemplate: Activity related to Baby Shark malware has been found on this asset.

A-Baby-Shark-Activity.ReasonTemplate: Activity related to Baby Shark malware has been found on this asset.
A-Baby-Shark-Activity.RuleDescription: Suspicious command line activity typically seen in Baby Shark malware has been found on this asset. Baby Shark malware can be used to exfiltrate system information, maintain persistence on a system, and allow further instruction from an attacker. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_babyshark.yml
A-Baby-Shark-Activity.RuleExpression: countByIf(command_line, asset,(containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'reg query "hkey_current_user\\software\\microsoft\\terminal server client\\default"', '- cmd.exe /c taskkill /im cmd.exe') || startsWith(toLower(command_line), 'powershell.exe mshta.exe http')), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-Baby-Shark-Activity')

A-Base64-CommandLine.AggregateReasonTemplate: Base64 string in command line argument from process: {default|event.process}
A-Base64-CommandLine.ReasonTemplate: Base64 string in command line argument from process: {default|event.process}
A-Base64-CommandLine.RuleDescription: A base64 string has been seen within a command line statement. Base64 strings are used to obfuscate data for transmission or other purposes. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_powershell_frombase64string.yml
A-Base64-CommandLine.RuleName: Base64 string in command line execution on this asset

A-Base64-Powershell-CmdLine-Keywords.AggregateReasonTemplate: Base64 encoded strings were found in hidden malicious Powershell command lines on this asset.
A-Base64-Powershell-CmdLine-Keywords.ReasonTemplate: Base64 encoded strings were found in hidden malicious Powershell command lines on this asset.
A-Base64-Powershell-CmdLine-Keywords.RuleDescription: Base64 encoded strings were found in hidden malicious Powershell command lines on this asset. This is notable because Powershell can be used to discover information or execute code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_powershell_hidden_b64_cmd.yml
A-Base64-Powershell-CmdLine-Keywords.RuleName: Base64 encoded strings were found in hidden malicious Powershell command lines on this asset.

A-Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.AggregateReasonTemplate: VBscript code referenced within a .bgi file was executed on this asset to bypass application whitelisting.
A-Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.ReasonTemplate: VBscript code referenced within a .bgi file was executed on this asset to bypass application whitelisting.
A-Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.RuleDescription: VBscript code referenced within a .bgi file was executed on this asset to bypass application whitelisting. This is notable as this method allows blindly trusted signed binaries to write code which can be leveraged to run malicious actions. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_bginfo.yml
A-Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.RuleName: VBscript referenced in a .bgi file was executed on this asset.

A-Bitsadmin-Download.AggregateReasonTemplate: Bitsadmin was used to start a file download on this asset.

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, ((toLower(process_name)='bitsadmin.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /transfer ')) or contains(toLower(command_line), 'copy bitsadmin.exe')), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-Bitsadmin-Download')

A-Bitsadmin-Download.ReasonTemplate: Bitsadmin was used to start a file download on this asset.
A-Bitsadmin-Download.RuleDescription: Bitsadmin was used to download a file on this asset. This is notable because Bitsadmin can be maliciously used to download, execute or clean up malicious payloads while enabling persistence. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_process_creation_bitsadmin_download.yml
A-Bitsadmin-Download.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, ((toLower(process_name)='bitsadmin.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /transfer ')) or contains(toLower(command_line), 'copy bitsadmin.exe')), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-Bitsadmin-Download')
A-Bitsadmin-Download.RuleName: Bitsadmin was used to download a file on this asset.

A-Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.AggregateReasonTemplate: Automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) had a child process on this asset.
A-Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.ReasonTemplate: Automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) had a child process on this asset.

This can be a legitimate usage of cmstp.exe by legitimate user but is still notable as cmstp.exe utilities can be used for malicious execution purposes or defense evasion. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_uac_cmstp.yml
A-Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.RuleName: Child process of automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) was created via command line on this asset.

A-CDB-App-Whitelisting.ReasonTemplate: 64-bit shellcode was launched from the x64_calc.wds file using cdb.exe on this asset to possibly bypass application whitelisting.
A-CDB-App-Whitelisting.RuleDescription: 64-bit shellcode was launched from the x64_calc.wds file using cdb.exe on this asset to possibly bypass application whitelisting. A-CDB-App-Whitelisting.RuleName: 64-bit shellcode was launched using cdb.exe on this asset.

A-CMD-Spawn-From-Office.ReasonTemplate: Microsoft Office application has spawned a command line executable
A-CMD-Spawn-From-Office.RuleDescription: A Microsoft Office application has spawned a command line process. This can indicate execution of malicious code. A-CP-Sensitive-Files.ReasonTemplate: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) were copied on this asset

A-CSC-Suspicious-Folder.ReasonTemplate: Csc.exe usage from suspicious folder, possible code execution

A-DCSync.ReasonTemplate: Domain Controller replication has occurred for a brand new domain controller / DCSync attack from a non-domain-controller is replicating AD information.
A-DCSync.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected that a new domain controller has joined the domain. This rule only triggers when a domain controller generates events indicating active directory domain replication is taking place for a newly joined domain controller. A DCSync attack has occurred if you have not added a new domain controller. This means that all active directory accounts and secrets have been copied to a non-domain controller workstation/machine. This attack is related to MITRE technique T1003.
A-DCSync.RuleExpression: countByIf(properties, dest_host, containsAny(toLower(properties), 'replicating directory changes all', '1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2', '9923a32a-3607-11d2-b9be-0000f87a36b2', '1131f6ac-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2', '1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2') && containsAny(object_type, '19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9','domainDNS'), 'ds-access')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-DCSync')
A-DCSync.RuleName: Possible DCSync Attack: New domain controller detected

A-DS-DCShadow.ReasonTemplate: Possible DCShadow attack. A machine,{default|event.src_host}, has performed an action that only newly created domain controllers perform.
A-DS-DCShadow.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected a newly joined domain controller. This may also be an indicator of a DCShadow attack. This rule only triggers when a new active directory object has been created indicating a brand new domain controller. When this occurs, all active directory information and secrets are copied to the new domain controller. Exabeam is flagging this because the specific events observed do not occur in a regular environment. In a DCShadow attack, the new machine may be able to modify active directory objects without raising alerts.
A-DS-DCShadow.RuleName: Possible DCShadow attack by asset detected.

A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j.AggregateReasonTemplate: FireWall disable arguments through command line detected on this asset.

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(command_line, dest_host, containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'susefirewall2 stop','resusefirewall2 stop','ufw stop','ufw disable'), 'process-created', 'process-created-failed', 'process-alert')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j')

A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j.ReasonTemplate: FireWall disable arguments through command line detected on this asset.
A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j.RuleDescription: A process tried to disable the firewall through command line on this asset. This is notable as these processes have commonly appeared in attempts to exploit the CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability.
A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j.RuleExpression: countByIf(command_line, dest_host, containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'susefirewall2 stop','resusefirewall2 stop','ufw stop','ufw disable'), 'process-created', 'process-created-failed', 'process-alert')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j')
A-KnownFirewallDisable-Log4j.RuleName: FireWall disable arguments via command line were detected on this asset.

A-Koadic-Tool-Usage.RuleDescription: 'Koadic' is an attacker tool used for post explotation. Exabeam has observed command line arguments used by this tool. This is notable as this can indicate an already compromised machine. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_hack_koadic.yml
A-Koadic-Tool-Usage.RuleName: 'Koadic' attacker tool usage on this asset

A-LSASS-Mem-Dump.ReasonTemplate: Lsass.exe memory space was dumped on this asset.
A-LSASS-Mem-Dump.RuleDescription: The LSASS memory space was accessed and credentials may have been dumped on this asset. lsass.exe is responsible for authentication in the domain, and handles sensitive credentials. Sysinternals procdump.exe was observed exporting the memory space of lsass.exe, meaning credentials may have been extracted, a sign of lateral movement. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_lsass_dump.yml
A-LSASS-Mem-Dump.RuleName: LSASS Memory Dumping detected on this asset

A-NSniff-Cred.ReasonTemplate: Detected network sniffing on this asset.
A-NSniff-Cred.RuleDescription: Potential network sniffing was observed on this asset. Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection. An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_network_sniffing.yml
A-NSniff-Cred.RuleName: Potential network sniffing was observed on this asset.

A-NotPetya-Activity.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible ransomeware, NotPetya, was detected on this asset.

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(process_name, dest_host,(toLower(process_name)='fsutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' deletejournal ')) || ((contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\.\\pipe\\')) || (toLower(process_name)='wevtutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' cl ')) || (toLower(process_name)='rundll32.exe' && endswith(toLower(command_line), '.dat,#1'))), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-NotPetya-Activity')

A-NotPetya-Activity.ReasonTemplate: Possible ransomeware, NotPetya, was detected on this asset.
A-NotPetya-Activity.RuleDescription: Artifacts of ransomware, NotPetya, were observed on this asset. Specifically, extracted passwords are passed back to the main module via named pipe, the file system journal of drive C is deleted and windows eventlogs are cleared using wevtutil. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_notpetya.yml
A-NotPetya-Activity.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, dest_host,(toLower(process_name)='fsutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' deletejournal ')) || ((contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\.\\pipe\\')) || (toLower(process_name)='wevtutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' cl ')) || (toLower(process_name)='rundll32.exe' && endswith(toLower(command_line), '.dat,#1'))), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-NotPetya-Activity')
A-NotPetya-Activity.RuleName: NotPetya Ransomware Activity detected on this asset

A-Odbcconf-DLL-Load.AggregateReasonTemplate: DLL loaded on this asset via odbcconf.exe execution.
A-Odbcconf-DLL-Load.ReasonTemplate: DLL loaded on this asset via odbcconf.exe execution.
A-Odbcconf-DLL-Load.RuleDescription: DLL loaded on this asset via odbcconf.exe execution. This is notable as Odbccond.exe allows the configuration of Open Database Conectivity drivers and is known to have a REGSVR flag that can be used to maliciously execute DLL files while avoiding detection. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_odbcconf.yml
A-Odbcconf-DLL-Load.RuleName: DLL loaded on this asset via odbcconf.exe execution.

Exabeam has marked this event as notable as Microsoft Office applications generally do not use the command line to download files from the internet, which is highly suspicious behavior. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_msoffice.yml
A-Office-Payload-Download.RuleName: Possible malicious payload download via Microsoft Office binaries on this asset

A-OpenWith-Exec-Cmd.ReasonTemplate: OpenWith.exe executed via command line on this asset.

A-WannaCry.AggregateReasonTemplate: Artifacts seen by WannaCry ransomware have been observed

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, (Inlist(toLower(process_name), 'tasksche.exe', 'mssecsvc.exe', 'taskdl.exe', 'taskhsvc.exe', 'taskse.exe', '111.exe', 'lhdfrgui.exe', 'linuxnew.exe', 'wannacry.exe')  || contains(toLower(process), 'wanadecryptor') || (contains(toLower(command_line),  'icacls ') && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /grant everyone:f /t /c /q')) || containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no', 'wbadmin delete catalog -quiet', '@please_read_me@.txt')), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-WannaCry')

A-WannaCry.ReasonTemplate: Artifacts seen by WannaCry ransomware have been observed
A-WannaCry.RuleDescription: WannaCry is ransomware. Known command line artifacts or known processes were detected. This event is notable as Wannacry is a dangerous worm that can quickly spread through networks on it's own. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_wannacry.yml
A-WannaCry.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, dest_host, (Inlist(toLower(process_name), 'tasksche.exe', 'mssecsvc.exe', 'taskdl.exe', 'taskhsvc.exe', 'taskse.exe', '111.exe', 'lhdfrgui.exe', 'linuxnew.exe', 'wannacry.exe')  || contains(toLower(process), 'wanadecryptor') || (contains(toLower(command_line),  'icacls ') && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /grant everyone:f /t /c /q')) || containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no', 'wbadmin delete catalog -quiet', '@please_read_me@.txt')), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-WannaCry')
A-WannaCry.RuleName: Artifacts seen by WannaCry malware have been observed on this asset

A-WebShell-CLI.ReasonTemplate: Possible command line web shell detected

A-WebShell-WebServer.RuleDescription: A web shell spawned from a web server has been observed. A web shell can help an attacker exfiltrate data as well as be used for C&C. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_webshell_spawn.yml
A-WebShell-WebServer.RuleName: Possible web server web shell detected on this asset

A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious parent process of well-known Windows processes was detected on this asset.

Aggregation.DataExpr: countByIf(process_name, asset, event_code='4688' && inList(toLower(process_name), 'svchost.exe','taskhost.exe','lsm.exe','lsass.exe','services.exe','lsaiso.exe','csrss.exe','wininit.exe','winlogon.exe') && !(containsAny(toLower(parent_process), '\\system32\\', '\\syswow64\\', '\\savservice.exe') || (contains(toLower(parent_process),'\\windows defender') && contains(toLower(parent_process),'\\msmpeng.exe'))) && exists(parent_process), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent')

A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious parent process of well-known Windows processes was detected on this asset.
A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.RuleDescription: A suspicious parent process of well-known Windows processes was detected on this asset. This could be an attempt to manipulate features of artifacts and make them appear legitimate or benign to evade defenses and observations. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_proc_wrong_parent.yml
A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.RuleExpression: countByIf(process_name, asset, event_code='4688' && inList(toLower(process_name), 'svchost.exe','taskhost.exe','lsm.exe','lsass.exe','services.exe','lsaiso.exe','csrss.exe','wininit.exe','winlogon.exe') && !(containsAny(toLower(parent_process), '\\system32\\', '\\syswow64\\', '\\savservice.exe') || (contains(toLower(parent_process),'\\windows defender') && contains(toLower(parent_process),'\\msmpeng.exe'))) && exists(parent_process), 'process-created')=1 && !WasRuleFired('A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent')
A-Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.RuleName: A suspicious parent process of well-known Windows processes was detected on this asset.

AS-PV-UsH-F.ReasonTemplate: First password retrieval from asset {asset|event.src|info} for user
AS-PV-UsH-F.RuleDescription: This event is notable because users typically access password vault from same assets.

AS-UA-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal switch to target account for user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
AS-UA-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal switch to target account {default|featureValue} for {user|event.user|histogram}
AS-UA-A.RuleDescription: A target credential is any credential that the primary, originating user has switched to. This is a notable event because it is abnormal for this user to switch to these specific credentials
AS-UA-A.RuleName: Abnormal switch to target account for user

AS-UA-F.ReasonTemplate: First switch to target account {default|featureValue} for {user|event.user|histogram}

AS-UA-FS.RuleDescription: This is the first time this user has ever switched credentials. While account switching is relatively common, it is worth noting when a user has done something they have never done before

ATP-AS-REP.AggregateReasonTemplate: UAC status change to disable preauthentication settings
ATP-AS-REP.ReasonTemplate: UAC status change to disable preauthentication settings
ATP-AS-REP.RuleDescription: There has been a UAC status change to disable preauthentication settings. This is notable because it is a known technique that could indicate AS-REP Roasting and should be investigated further.
ATP-AS-REP.RuleExpression: contains(event_code, '4738') and contains(toLower(uac_status_new), 'dont require preauth – enabled') && !WasRuleFired('ATP-AS-REP')
ATP-AS-REP.RuleName: Suspicious UAC status change indicating AS-REP Roasting

ATP-AS-REP-2.AggregateReasonTemplate: UAC directory service change indicating AS-REP Roasting
ATP-AS-REP-2.ReasonTemplate: UAC directory service change indicating AS-REP Roasting
ATP-AS-REP-2.RuleDescription: There have been directory service changes. This is notable because they are performed whenever UAC settings are changed on the domain indicative of AS-REP Roasting and should be investigated further.
ATP-AS-REP-2.RuleName: Suspicious UAC directory service change indicating AS-REP Roasting

ATP-AS-REP-3.AggregateReasonTemplate: User doesn't require a pre-authentication to the server
ATP-AS-REP-3.ReasonTemplate: User doesn't require a pre-authentication to the server
ATP-AS-REP-3.RuleDescription: First time user has logged on via Kerberos authentication with preauthentication as 0. This is notableas it indicates a user doesn't need to authenticate to the server with password and this is a known method of the AS-AEP Kerberoasting attack
ATP-AS-REP-3.RuleName: First Kerberos logon for abnormal pre-authentication type for the user

ATP-FTP-Exfil.ReasonTemplate: User executed {default|featureValue} to run scripts on the host
ATP-FTP-Exfil.RuleDescription: Ftp.exe is used to run scripts on the host. This is notable since attackers often use ftp to run a file hosted on a server.

ATP-GsecDump.AggregateReasonTemplate: First credential dumping GsecDump service installed on host: {default|featureValue}
ATP-GsecDump.ReasonTemplate: First credential dumping GsecDump service installed on host: {default|featureValue}
ATP-GsecDump.RuleDescription: The use ran their first GsecDump service. This is notable because it is a credential dumping service and should be further investigated
ATP-GsecDump.RuleName: First GsecDump service was run by this user.

ATP-PSexec.AggregateReasonTemplate: PSExec service was run on the asset by this user.
ATP-PSexec.ReasonTemplate: PSExec service was run on the asset by this user.
ATP-PSexec.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted psexec service was run on the host which is used to run something on a remote server folder. This is notable as this is a known method of the HAFNIUM actor responsible for the Microsoft Exchange vulnerability exploits.
ATP-PSexec.RuleName: PSExec service was run on the asset by this user.

ATP-PWDump.AggregateReasonTemplate: alicious process/file was run from a temp folder: {default|featureValue}
ATP-PWDump.ReasonTemplate: Sensitive process {default|event.process_name} was run from a temp folder
ATP-PWDump.RuleDescription: A malicious exe was run from a temp folder which is a part of pwdump credential dumping tool. This is notable because dumping credentials is a way to obtain login and credential information which can be used to perform lateral movement or access restricted information.
ATP-PWDump.RuleName: Malicious exe was run which is a part of credential dumping tool

ATP-REG-Password.ReasonTemplate: Reg.exe was used to extract password from the hives.

ATP-WMIC-Antivirus.AggregateReasonTemplate: Microsoft utility {default|featureValue} is used to extract antivirus information
ATP-WMIC-Antivirus.ReasonTemplate: Microsoft utility {default|event.parent_process_name} is used to extract antivirus information
ATP-WMIC-Antivirus.RuleDescription: There has been an antivirus detection using MSBuild which is used to get details for Antivirus installed on the system.
ATP-WMIC-Antivirus.RuleName: Antivirus detection using windows utility msbuild.

AUTH-F-COUNT.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of failed authentications for user
AUTH-F-COUNT.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of failed authentications ({quantity|featureValue}), expected around ({quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram})
AUTH-F-COUNT.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that this user has an order of magnitude more authentication failures than usual. This event is notable since it may indicate use of stolen credentials
AUTH-F-COUNT.RuleName: Abnormal number of failed authentications for user

AccountDiscovery.RuleDescription: Enumerating account information can aid an attacker in directing his attacks against certain users. Exabeam has identified commands that extract this type of account information. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_local_system_owner_account_discovery.yml
AccountDiscovery.RuleExpression: ((((InList(toLower(process_name), 'whoami.exe', 'quser.exe', 'qwinsta.exe')) || (toLower(process_name)='wmic.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), 'useraccount') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'get')) || (toLower(process_name)='cmdkey.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), '/list')) or (toLower(process_name)='cmd.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), '/c') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'dir ') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\users\\'))) && !contains(toLower(command_line), ' rmdir ')) || (InList(toLower(process_name), 'net.exe', 'net1.exe') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'user') && !containsany(toLower(command_line), '/domain', '/add', '/delete', '/active', '/expires', '/passwordreq', '/scriptpath', '/times', '/workstations'))) && !WasRuleFired('AccountDiscovery')

Applocker-Bypass.ReasonTemplate: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker.
Applocker-Bypass.RuleDescription: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker whitelisting were performed. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_possible_applocker_bypass.yml
Applocker-Bypass.RuleName: Execution of executables that can be used to bypass Applocker

Archer.ReasonTemplate: Known malware, 'Archer', has been executed by the 'rundll32' executable

Auth-Tor-Shost-Failed.ReasonTemplate: Failed login/authentication from a known TOR IP, {default|featureValue}.

AutoRun-Modification.RuleDescription: Reg.exe was used to directly modify the 'Autostart Extensibility Point (ASEP)' software. This change affects what software is automatically run without user interaction. This event is notable as this technique can allow attackers to run unstrusted code and avoid detection. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_direct_asep_reg_keys_modification.yml

B-CS-Bucket-Activity-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal to see this specific container/bucket-operation on this container/bucket
B-CS-Bucket-Activity-A.RuleName: Abnormal type of object access against this bucket

B-CS-Bucket-Activity-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this activity, {default|featureValue|histogram}, on this storage container/bucket
B-CS-Bucket-Activity-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this activity, {default|featureValue|histogram}, on this storage container/bucket
B-CS-Bucket-Activity-F.RuleDescription: This is time seeing this specific object operation against this bucket.
B-CS-Bucket-Activity-F.RuleName: First type of object access against this bucket

B-CS-Bucket-Bytes-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal amount of egress data from bucket: ({bytes|featureValue}), expected around {bytes|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-Bytes-A.RuleDescription: An abnormal amount of egress data was observed for this bucket. Some storage containers/buckets have a consistent amount of data being accessed. Exabeam has observed that for this sequence, the amount of egress data seen deviates from the normal amount.
B-CS-Bucket-Bytes-A.RuleName: Abnormal amount of egress data from bucket

B-CS-Bucket-UA-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: User agent accessing this bucket is abnormal: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-UA-A.ReasonTemplate: User agent accessing this bucket is abnormal: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-UA-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal to see this user agent when accessing this bucket. When accessing cloud storage buckets/containers, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud storage. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise, leading to exfiltration of data.
B-CS-Bucket-UA-A.RuleName: Abnormal user agent access to this bucket, possible exfiltration

B-CS-Bucket-UA-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time this bucket accessed by this user agent: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-UA-F.ReasonTemplate: First time this bucket accessed using this user agent: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-UA-F.RuleDescription: This is if the first time this user agent was seen during access of this bucket. When accessing cloud storage buckets/containers, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud storage. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise, leading to exfiltration of data.
B-CS-Bucket-UA-F.RuleName: New user agent has accessed this bucket, possible exfiltration

B-CS-Bucket-Users-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal user: {default|featureValue|histogram} accessing this storage container
B-CS-Bucket-Users-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user: {default|featureValue|histogram} accessing this storage container
B-CS-Bucket-Users-A.RuleDescription: It is not normal for this user to be accessing this storage container/bucket. Buckets generally have a regular pattern of users that access a storage caontainer/bucket. Access by an abnormal user can indicate compromised credentials or exfiltration.
B-CS-Bucket-Users-A.RuleName: Abnormal user accessing this storage container/bucket

B-CS-Bucket-Users-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First access to bucket by user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-Users-F.ReasonTemplate: First access to bucket by user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Bucket-Users-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this bucket has been accessed by this user. Buckets generally have a regular pattern of users that access a storage caontainer/bucket. Access by a user for the first time can indicate compromised credentials or exfiltration.
B-CS-Bucket-Users-F.RuleName: First time for user to access this bucket

B-CS-Buckets-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First Cloud Storage bucket is seen in the org: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Buckets-F.ReasonTemplate: First time Cloud Storage bucket is seen in the org: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-Buckets-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this cloud storage bucket has been seen in the organization. New buckets can be used to stage files for later exfiltration.
B-CS-Buckets-F.RuleName: First cloud storage/bucket in the organization

B-CS-UType-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal user type accessing  this bucket: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-UType-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user type accessing this bucket: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-UType-A.RuleDescription: Normally this bucket is accessed by certain kinds of users. A seldom seen user type is notable. This specific user type does not normally access this bucket, and can indicate a difference in how the bucket is being used.
B-CS-UType-A.RuleName: Abnormal for this user type to access this bucket

B-CS-UType-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this user type to access this bucket: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-UType-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this user type to access this bucket: {default|featureValue|histogram}
B-CS-UType-F.RuleDescription: A new type of user has accessed this bucket. Normally this bucket is accessed by certain kinds of users. A new usertype is notable as it can indicate a usage change for the bucket.
B-CS-UType-F.RuleName: First time this specific user type has accessed this bucket

BITS-Suspicious-Service.AggregateReasonTemplate: First abnormal BITS job created using process: {default|event.process_name}
BITS-Suspicious-Service.ReasonTemplate: First abnormal BITS job created using process: {default|event.process_name}
BITS-Suspicious-Service.RuleDescription: A BITS job was created on the endpoint to transfer/create an unknown file from an unknown server. This is notable as BITS jobs can be used to maintain persistence or evade detection by removing malicious payloads.
BITS-Suspicious-Service.RuleName: First abnormal BITS jobs created on the endpoint

Baby-Shark-Activity.AggregateReasonTemplate: Activity related to Baby Shark malware has been found.
Baby-Shark-Activity.ReasonTemplate: Activity related to Baby Shark malware has been found.
Baby-Shark-Activity.RuleDescription: Suspicious command line activity typically seen in Baby Shark malware has been found. Baby Shark malware can be used to exfiltrate system information, maintain persistence on a system, and allow further instruction from an attacker. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_babyshark.yml
Baby-Shark-Activity.RuleExpression: (containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'reg query "hkey_current_user\\software\\microsoft\\terminal server client\\default"', '- cmd.exe /c taskkill /im cmd.exe') || startsWith(toLower(command_line), 'powershell.exe mshta.exe http')) && !WasRuleFired('Baby-Shark-Activity')
Baby-Shark-Activity.RuleName: Activity related to Baby Shark malware has been found.

Base64-CommandLine.AggregateReasonTemplate: Base64 string in command line argument from process: {default|event.process}
Base64-CommandLine.ReasonTemplate: Base64 string in command line argument from process: {default|event.process}

Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.ReasonTemplate: VBscript code referenced within a .bgi file was executed to bypass application whitelisting.
Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.RuleDescription: VBscript code referenced within a .bgi file was executed to bypass application whitelisting. This is notable as this method allows blindly trusted signed binaries to write code which can be leveraged to run malicious actions. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_bginfo.yml
Bginfo-App-Whitelisting.RuleName: VBscript referenced in a .bgi file was executed.

Bitsadmin-Download.AggregateReasonTemplate: Bitsadmin was used to start a file download.
Bitsadmin-Download.ReasonTemplate: Bitsadmin was used to start a file download.
Bitsadmin-Download.RuleDescription: Bitsadmin was used to download a file. This is notable because Bitsadmin can be maliciously used to download, execute or clean up malicious payloads while enabling persistence. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_process_creation_bitsadmin_download.yml
Bitsadmin-Download.RuleName: Bitsadmin was used to download a file.

Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.ReasonTemplate: Automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) had a child process.
Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.RuleDescription: Child process of automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) was created via command line. This can be a legitimate usage of cmstp.exe by legitimate user but is still notable as cmstp.exe utilities can be used for malicious execution purposes or defense evasion. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_uac_cmstp.yml
Bypass-UAC-CMSTP.RuleName: Child process of automatically elevated instance of Microsoft Connection Manager Profile Installer (cmstp.exe) was created via command line.

CA-UniversalPolicy-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user:{default|featureValue|histogram} to handle a known dangerous policy config
CA-UniversalPolicy-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for this user to handle/attach '*' policy. This type of policy represents universal access to whatever cloud object this policy becomes attached to. This is a dangerous configuration that can allow unwanted access, and should be further scrutinized.
CA-UniversalPolicy-A.RuleName: Abnormal for this user to create/attach a 'universal' resource/action policy

CA-UniversalPolicy-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this user: {default|featureValue|histogram} to handle a known dangerous policy config
CA-UniversalPolicy-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this user:{default|featureValue|histogram} to handle a known dangerous policy config
CA-UniversalPolicy-F.RuleDescription: A '*' policy was created or attached to an object. This type of policy represents universal access to whatever cloud object this policy becomes attached to. This is a dangerous configuration that can allow unwanted access, and should be further scrutinized.
CA-UniversalPolicy-F.RuleName: First time this user has created/attached a 'universal' resource/action policy

CDB-App-Whitelisting.ReasonTemplate: 64-bit shellcode was launched from the x64_calc.wds file using cdb.exe to possibly bypass application whitelisting.

CMD-Spawn-From-Office.ReasonTemplate: Microsoft Office application has spawned a command line executable
CMD-Spawn-From-Office.RuleDescription: A Microsoft Office application has spawned a command line process. This can indicate execution of malicious code. Office applications are popular infection vectors for attackers, making this event notable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_office_shell.yml
CMD-Spawn-From-Office.RuleName: A command line executable was spawned from an Office application

CP-Sensitive-Files.AggregateReasonTemplate: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) were copied
CP-Sensitive-Files.ReasonTemplate: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) were copied
CP-Sensitive-Files.RuleDescription: Files with well-known filenames (sensitive files with credential data) were copied. Certain sensitive files should never be accessed or copied, therefore this is notable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_copying_sensitive_files_with_credential_data.yml
CP-Sensitive-Files.RuleName: Copying sensitive files with credential data

CS-Admin-Activity-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for this user to invoke this specific Cloud Admin activity. Operations that are rarely performed should be scrutinized, as certain admin operations can provide vast operational value for an attacker.
CS-Admin-Activity-A.RuleName: Abnormal invocation of this specific admin activity

CS-Admin-Activty-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this Cloud Administrative activity: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Admin-Activty-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this Cloud Administrative activity: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Admin-Activty-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this user has performed this specific Cloud administrative activity. Cloud administrative operations control all aspects of the cloud environment, and a never before seen operation could indicate an attack against cloud resources.
CS-Admin-Activty-F.RuleName: First time seeing this Cloud administrative operation

CS-Bucket-C-D-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for user to create/delete Cloud bucket: {default|event.bucket}
CS-Bucket-C-D-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for user to create/delete Cloud bucket: {default|event.bucket}
CS-Bucket-C-D-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time for this user to create or delete a bucket. Creating a brand new bucket can indicate the beginning of an attack in a cloud environment by utilizing a brand new bucket to store and/or exfiltrate files. Deleting a bucket can indicate erasing the cloud log trail.
CS-Bucket-C-D-F.RuleExpression: num_observations=0 && ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual() && ((contains(vendor,'AWS') && InList(toLower(activity),'createbucket','deletebucket')) ||(contains(vendor,'Azure') && (containsAny(toLower(activity),'put blob container', 'delete blob container', 'put file share', 'delete file share') || (containsAny(toLower(activity), 'write','create') && contains(toLower(activity), 'containers')))) || (contains(vendor,'Google') && containsAny(toLower(activity),'buckets.insert','buckets.delete'))) && !WasRuleFired('CS-Bucket-C-D-F',activity)
CS-Bucket-C-D-F.RuleName: Cloud Storage bucket/storage container creation/deletion for the first time

CS-Bucket-Created.RuleDescription: A cloud storage bucket/container was created. This event alone is not notable, however, creating buckets is an important activity that should be tracked.
CS-Bucket-Created.RuleExpression: ((contains(vendor,'AWS') && InList(toLower(activity),'createbucket','deletebucket')) ||(contains(vendor,'Azure') && (containsAny(toLower(activity),'put blob container', 'delete blob container', 'put file share', 'delete file share') || (containsAny(toLower(activity), 'write','create') && contains(toLower(activity), 'containers')))) || (contains(vendor,'Google') && containsAny(toLower(activity),'buckets.insert','buckets.delete'))) && !WasRuleFired('CS-Bucket-Created')

CS-Bucket-UA-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: User agent accessing bucket is abnormal
CS-Bucket-UA-A.ReasonTemplate: User agent accessing this bucket is abnormal: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Bucket-UA-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal to see this user agent when accessing this bucket. When accessing cloud storage buckets/containers, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud storage. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise, leading to exfiltration of data.
CS-Bucket-UA-A.RuleName: Abnormal user agent access for bucket

CS-Bucket-UA-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time this bucket accessed by this user agent
CS-Bucket-UA-F.ReasonTemplate: First time this bucket accessed using this user agent: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Bucket-UA-F.RuleDescription: This is if the first time this user agent was seen during access of this bucket. When accessing cloud storage buckets/containers, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud storage. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise, leading to exfiltration of data.
CS-Bucket-UA-F.RuleName: New user agent access for bucket

CS-Critical-Activity-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal user: {default|featureValue|histogram} performing a critical Cloud Administrative operation: {default|event.activity}
CS-Critical-Activity-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user: {default|featureValue|histogram} performing a critical Cloud Administrative operation: {default|event.activity}
CS-Critical-Activity-A.RuleDescription: This rule tracks the operations of attaching/detaching a policy to an object, and the creation of an access key. Policies define the ACL attributes for an object and the users accessing that object. Removing or adding policies can indicate an attempt to move laterally or access confidential resources. A new access key can be used for persistence or lateral movement, as an access key allows an attacker to access cloud resources from a brand new authorization credential set, potentially evading detection.
CS-Critical-Activity-A.RuleExpression: ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual() && num_observations>0 && num_observations<percentile_threshold_count && ((contains(vendor,'AWS') && InList(toLower(activity),'createaccesskey','attachuserpolicy','dettachuserpolicy')) || (contains(vendor,'Azure') && containsAny(toLower(activity),'set administrator','delete-administrator', 'classicadministrators', 'role definition','role assignment', 'policyassignments', 'removeactivatedrole', 'createrequest')) || (contains(vendor, 'Google') && InList(toLower(activity), 'setiampolicy', 'clearorgpolicy')))
CS-Critical-Activity-A.RuleName: Abnormal user to perform a critical Cloud Administrative operation

CS-Critical-Activity-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for {default|featureValue|histogram} performing a critical Cloud Administrative operation: {default|event.activity}
CS-Critical-Activity-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for {default|featureValue|histogram} performing a critical Cloud Administrative operation: {default|event.activity}
CS-Critical-Activity-F.RuleDescription: This rule tracks the operations of attaching/detaching a policy to an object, and the creation of an access key. Policies define the ACL attributes for an object and the users accessing that object. Removing or adding policies can indicate an attempt to move laterally or access confidential resources. A new access key can be used for persistence or lateral movement, as an access key allows an attacker to access cloud resources from a brand new authorization credential set, potentially evading detection.
CS-Critical-Activity-F.RuleExpression: ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual() && num_observations=0 && ((contains(vendor,'AWS') && InList(toLower(activity),'createaccesskey','attachuserpolicy','dettachuserpolicy')) || (contains(vendor,'Azure') && containsAny(toLower(activity),'set administrator','delete-administrator', 'classicadministrators', 'role definition','role assignment', 'policyassignments', 'removeactivatedrole', 'createrequest')) || (contains(vendor, 'Google Cloud') && InList(toLower(activity), 'setiampolicy', 'clearorgpolicy')))
CS-Critical-Activity-F.RuleName: First time for this user to perform a critical Cloud Administrative operation

CS-Failed-User-Creation.AggregateReasonTemplate: User attempted and failed to create a Cloud account
CS-Failed-User-Creation.ReasonTemplate: User attempted and failed to create a Cloud account
CS-Failed-User-Creation.RuleDescription: This user attempted and failed to create a user account. Users generally know whether their accounts are authorized to create an account. Account creation that fails is suspicious because it can indicate an attempt to establish persistence.
CS-Failed-User-Creation.RuleName: User attempted and failed to create a Cloud user/account

CS-IAM-Enumeration.RuleDescription: This user listed the users or roles in the cloud organization. Enumerating cloud objects such as users and roles (special accounts that users can assume/elevate to in order to perform certain actions) can aid an attacker in moving laterally by understanding what users and attached permissions can aid in the attacker's operations.

CS-Policies-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for this policy to be used. Policies define access controls for the objects/users the policies are attached to. The usage of a rarely used policy can indicate an attempt to access resources that should not be accessed by this user.

CS-Policies-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time seeing this cloud policy: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Policies-F.ReasonTemplate: First time seeing this cloud policy: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Policies-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this cloud policy has been seen. Policies define access controls for the objects/users the policies are attached to. A new policy can indicate an attempt to access resources that should not be accessed by this user.
CS-Policies-F.RuleName: First time seeing this cloud policy

CS-S3-Enumeration.AggregateReasonTemplate: User enumerated Cloud Storage:{default|event.vendor} containers/files using: {default|event.activity}
CS-S3-Enumeration.ReasonTemplate: User enumerated Cloud Storage:{default|event.vendor} containers/files using: {default|event.activity}
CS-S3-Enumeration.RuleDescription: This user listed buckets in the cloud storage service. Enumerating cloud objects such as buckets or the objects within the buckets can take place in an attacker's process of exfiltration of data.

CS-Storage-Activity-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal activity against cloud storage service/objects: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Storage-Activity-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal activity against cloud storage service/objects: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Storage-Activity-A.RuleDescription: This if the first time this user has invoked this specific activity against the cloud storage service or against a cloud storage object. A never before seen operation by a user against the cloud storage service can indicate compromised credentials, as new activity can exhibit behavior that an individual account normally would not perform.
CS-Storage-Activity-A.RuleName: Abnormal activity against the cloud storage service

CS-Storage-Activity-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this activity against cloud storage service/objects: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Storage-Activity-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this activity against cloud storage service/objects: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-Storage-Activity-F.RuleDescription: This if the first time this user has invoked this specific activity against the cloud storage service or against a cloud storage object. A never before seen operation by a user against the cloud storage service can indicate compromised credentials, as new activity can exhibit behavior that an individual account normally would not perform.
CS-Storage-Activity-F.RuleName: First time using this event activity against the cloud storage service

CS-UA-O-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal user agent accessing cloud storage services: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-O-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user agent accessing cloud storage services: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-O-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal to observe this user agent being used to access cloud services. When accessing cloud services, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud services. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise.
CS-UA-O-A.RuleName: Abnormal user agent accessing cloud services in the organization

CS-UA-O-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time this user agent: {default|featureValue|histogram} has been seen for the organization
CS-UA-O-F.ReasonTemplate: First time this user agent: {default|featureValue|histogram} has been seen for the organization
CS-UA-O-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time Exabeam has observed this user agent access cloud services. When accessing cloud services, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud storage service. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise.
CS-UA-O-F.RuleName: First user agent to access cloud services in the organization

CS-UA-P-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: User agent for peer group used to access cloud services is abnormal: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-P-A.ReasonTemplate: User agent for peer group used to access cloud services is abnormal: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-P-A.RuleDescription: This user agent is abnormal for this peer group to use when accessing cloud services. When accessing cloud services, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud services. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise.
CS-UA-P-A.RuleName: Abnormal user agent for the peer group accessing cloud service

CS-UA-P-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time for this peer group to user this user agent against cloud services: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-P-F.ReasonTemplate: First time for this peer group to user this user agent against cloud services: {default|featureValue|histogram}
CS-UA-P-F.RuleDescription: This is if the first time this peer group has used this user agent string when accessing cloud services. When accessing cloud services, a user agent can be seen as a 'fingerprint' for how that account or user accesses cloud services. A new 'fingerprint' can indicate possible account/credential compromise.
CS-UA-P-F.RuleName: First user agent for peer group to access cloud services

CS-User-Creation-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time this user {default|featureValue|histogram} has performed Cloud account creation activity: {user|event.identity}
CS-User-Creation-F.ReasonTemplate: First time this user {default|featureValue|histogram} has performed Cloud account creation activity: {user|event.identity}
CS-User-Creation-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this user has attempted to create an account. Normally only certain users create accounts, making this event notable. Account creation can aid attackers in hiding their activity because some accounts may be less monitorired. By using an account with different privileges, an attacker may be able to establish persistence.
CS-User-Creation-F.RuleName: First time for this user to create an account in the cloud

CS-Users-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal user:{default|featureValue|histogram} accessing cloud storage services/objects
CS-Users-A.ReasonTemplate: Abmormal user:{default|featureValue|histogram} accessing cloud storage services/objects
CS-Users-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal to see this username accessing the organzation's cloud storage account / objects
CS-Users-A.RuleName: Abnormal user is seen accessing the cloud storage service

CS-Users-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time seeing user:{default|featureValue|histogram} accessing cloud storage services/objects
CS-Users-F.ReasonTemplate: First time seeing user:{default|featureValue|histogram} accessing cloud storage services/objects
CS-Users-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time this username was seen accessing the organization's cloud storage account / objects
CS-Users-F.RuleName: First time this user is seen accessing the cloud storage service

CSC-Suspicious-Folder.ReasonTemplate: Csc.exe usage from suspicious folder, possible code execution

CSharp-Interactive-Console.ReasonTemplate: Execution of CSharp interactive console by PowerShell.

CertUtil-Suspicious-Usage.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious command line flags related to certutil normally used to decode downloaded files

DCSync.AggregateReasonTemplate: Domain Controller replication has occurred for a brand new domain controller / DCSync attack from a non-domain-controller is replicating AD information.
DCSync.ReasonTemplate: Domain Controller replication has occurred for a brand new domain controller / DCSync attack from a non-domain-controller is replicating AD information.
DCSync.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected that active directory data has been replicated in a way only seen when new domain controllers are added to the domain. This rule only triggers when an existing domain controller generates events indicating its active directory data is being replicated to a newly joined domain controller OR a DCSync attack has occurred. A DCSync attack has occurred if you have not added a new domain controller. This means that all active directory accounts and secrets have been copied to a non-domain controller workstation/machine. This attack is related to MITRE technique T1003.

DCSync-ExistHost.AggregateReasonTemplate: Domain Controller replication from a well-established host.
DCSync-ExistHost.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected an existing machine replicating the Active Directory. This alert only triggers if all the indicators that a DCSync attack/newly joined/promoted Domain Controller has occurred. This is extremely unusual, as this host has already been seen before, and it is not normal for an existing host to become a Domain Controller. This should not occur, as the events generated to trigger this rule only occur when a host is actively being promoted to Domain Controller, which generally does not happen to already existing hosts. There is a high probability that a DCSync attack is taking place. This attack is related to MITRE technique T1003.
DCSync-ExistHost.RuleName: Possible DCSync attack - existing host has replicated Active Directory.

DCSync-FirstDS.AggregateReasonTemplate: DC replication events have not previously been seen for this host.
DCSync-FirstDS.ReasonTemplate: Domain Controller replication events have not been seen for this host, {default|featureValue|histogram}.
DCSync-FirstDS.RuleDescription: This rule has triggered on an already suspected DCSync attack. A new indicator, that the source host has not generated this directory service event before, has been detected. Exabeam has high confidence that a DCSync attack has taken place, meaning all Active Directory accounts and secrets have been replicated to a non Domain Controller. The 'keys to the kingdom' may have been stolen! Please follow up on this. This attack is related to MITRE technique T1003.
DCSync-FirstDS.RuleName: Possible DCSync attack - first DS access event from host.

DS-DCSh-Add.ReasonTemplate: A directory service server object ({default|featureValue}) has been created.
DS-DCSh-Add.RuleDescription: A directory service server object has been created. The presence of this rule trigger does not indicate anything malicious, and on it's own does not present any immediate risk. This rule tracks when a directory server has been stood up. This event itself is notable as a directory service server object being stood up is rare event.

DS-DCSh-Del.ReasonTemplate: A directory service server object ({default|featureValue}) has been created and deleted.
DS-DCSh-Del.RuleDescription: A directory service server object has been created and deleted in the same session. Both adding and deleting a DS server object is highly unusual, and is a trait of DC Shadow attack. This may indicate that a machine may have replicated all DS secerets and keys. This attack is related to MITRE technique T1003.
DS-DCSh-Del.RuleName: Directory service server object created and deleted

DS-DCShadow.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible DCShadow attack. Host {default|event.src_host} has performed an action that only newly created domain controllers perform.
DS-DCShadow.ReasonTemplate: Possible DCShadow attack. Host {default|event.src_host} has performed an action that only newly created domain controllers perform.
DS-DCShadow.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected a newly joined domain controller. This may also be an indicator of a DCShadow attack. This rule only triggers when a new active directory object has been created indicating a brand new domain controller. When this occurs, all active directory information and secrets are copied to the new domain controller. Exabeam is flagging this because the specific events observed do not occur regularly. In a DCShadow attack, the new machine may be able to modify active directory objects without raising alerts.

DS-DCShadow-E.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible DCShadow attack. Machine with existing history, {default|event.src_host|histogram}, performing Domain Controller specific actions.
DS-DCShadow-E.ReasonTemplate: Possible DCShadow attack: machine with existing history, {default|event.src_host|histogram}, performing Domain Controller specific actions.
DS-DCShadow-E.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected that a machine with significant history is performing events normally only observed by a newly registered Domain Controller. This is notable as the events observed only come from newly activated machines, not an already existing one. This is a very high indication that possible DCShadow attack has occurred. This means that all Active Directory objects, including all secrets, have been copied to a new machine. In a DCShadow attack, the new machine may be able to modify active directory objects without raising alerts.
DS-DCShadow-E.RuleName: Possible DCShadow attack from Existing Machine

DS-DCShadow-F.ReasonTemplate: First {default|featureValue|histogram} event for {default|scopeValue} in a possible DCShadow attack
DS-DCShadow-F.RuleDescription: Exabeam has detected that a machine has performed this class of directory service events for the first time. This is another indicator of a DCShadow as an existing host is performing this type of event for the first time. This is notable as legitimate Domain Controllers generate this type of activity frequently.
DS-DCShadow-F.RuleName: First event for machine in possible DCShadow attack

Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_slingshot.yml

EPA-RAT-TI.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that this user has installed TeamViewer software, which is a remote desktop access service that allows remote access to a system through browser. This event can be an indicator of malicious activity that aims at establishing a reverse connection to an adversary controlled system.
EPA-RAT-TI.RuleName: TeamViewer remote desktop access agent installed by this user

EPA-RAT-TSI.AggregateReasonTemplate: TeamViewer remote desktop access service installed by this user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-RAT-TSI.ReasonTemplate: TeamViewer remote desktop access service installed by this user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-RAT-TSI.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that this user has installed TeamViewer service. TeamViewer is a remote desktop access service that allows remote access to a system through browser. This event can be an indicator of malicious activity that aims at establishing a reverse connection to an adversary controlled system.
EPA-RAT-TSI.RuleName: TeamViewer remote desktop access service installed by this user

EPA-RAT-TSS.AggregateReasonTemplate: TeamViewer remote desktop access service started by this user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-RAT-TSS.ReasonTemplate: TeamViewer remote desktop access service started by this user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-RAT-TSS.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that this user has started running TeamViewer service. TeamViewer is a remote desktop access service that allows remote access to a system through browser. This event can be an indicator of malicious activity that aims at establishing a reverse connection to an adversary controlled system.
EPA-RAT-TSS.RuleName: TeamViewer remote desktop access service started by this user

EPA-SERVICE-PARAMS.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious parameters found in process for service creation for the user: {default|event.process}
EPA-SERVICE-PARAMS.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious parameters found in process: {default|event.process} for service creation for the user
EPA-SERVICE-PARAMS.RuleDescription: It is suspicious to use these parameters in service installation process
EPA-SERVICE-PARAMS.RuleName: Suspicious parameters found in process for service creation

EPA-SNIFF.AggregateReasonTemplate: Network sniffing tool run by this user
EPA-SNIFF.ReasonTemplate: Network sniffing tool tool run by this user
EPA-SNIFF.RuleDescription: Exabeam has seen this user running a network sniffing tool. Network sniffing can be used to get information about an environment including authentication materials, configuration details, and other network information often used in Lateral Movement and/or Defense Evasion activities.
EPA-SNIFF.RuleName: Network sniffing tool has been run by this user

EPA-Shadow-Mining-name.AggregateReasonTemplate: User execution of process: {default|event.process}, ending with 'miner.exe', possible cryptocurrency miner
EPA-Shadow-Mining-name.ReasonTemplate: User execution of process: {default|event.process}, ending with 'miner.exe', possible cryptocurrency miner
EPA-Shadow-Mining-name.RuleDescription: User has executed a process with the process name ending with the string 'miner.exe'. Many crytocurrency mining software executables end in this fashion. Crytocurreng mining is cause for concern due to the ability to generate revenue for attackers.
EPA-Shadow-Mining-name.RuleName: Process ending with 'miner.exe' has been run

EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Process has been executed from a temporary directory: {default|featureValue} during endpoint activity
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal process {default|event.process_name|histogram} has been executed from a temporary directory by this user during endpoint activity
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-A.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this process has been executed from a temporary directory. Processes normally run from their installation directory and not from temporary or cache directories and therefore this event is notable.
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-A.RuleName: Abnormal process has been executed from a temporary directory by this user during endpoint activity

EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time process has been executed from a temporary directory: {default|featureValue} during endpoint activity
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-F.ReasonTemplate: First time process {default|event.process_name|histogram} has been executed from a temporary directory by this user during endpoint activity
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-F.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this process has been executed from a temporary directory. Processes normally run from their installation directory and not from temporary or cache directories and therefore this event is notable.
EPA-TEMP-DIRECTORY-F.RuleName: First time process has been executed from a temporary directory by this user during endpoint activity

EPA-UD-DGA.AggregateReasonTemplate: INTERNAL: User has accessed a domain through network that has been identified as DGA: {default|featureValue}
EPA-UD-DGA.ReasonTemplate: User has accessed domain {default|event.web_domain} through network that has been identified as DGA
EPA-UD-DGA.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this user has attempted to access a web domain that seems to be DGA (Domain Generating Algorithm) generated. It is a common practice for malware to establish communications over a pseudo random domain name that is generated by an algorithm, an access to such domain be indicative of malware communicating outside of the network.
EPA-UD-DGA.RuleName: INTERNAL: User has accessed a domain through network that has been identified as DGA

EPA-UD-DGA-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UD-DGA-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal access to this domain {default|event.web_domain|histogram} through network which has been identified as DGA
EPA-UD-DGA-A.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this user has attempted to access a web domain that seems to be DGA (Domain Generating Algorithm) generated. It is a common practice for malware to establish communications over a pseudo random domain name that is generated by an algorithm, an access to such domain be indicative of malware communicating outside of the network.
EPA-UD-DGA-A.RuleName: Abnormal access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA

EPA-UD-DGA-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UD-DGA-F.ReasonTemplate: First access to this domain {default|event.web_domain|histogram} through network which has been identified as DGA
EPA-UD-DGA-F.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this user has attempted to access a web domain that seems to be DGA (Domain Generating Algorithm) generated.
