EPA-UD-DGA-F.RuleName: First access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA

EPA-UD-DGA-N.AggregateReasonTemplate: Common access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UD-DGA-N.ReasonTemplate: Common access to this domain {default|event.web_domain|histogram} through network which has been identified as DGA
EPA-UD-DGA-N.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected that this user has attempted to access a web domain that seems to be DGA (Domain Generating Algorithm) generated. It is a common practice for malware to establish communications over a pseudo random domain name that is generated by an algorithm, an access to such domain be indicative of malware communicating outside of the network.
EPA-UD-DGA-N.RuleName: Common access to this domain through network which has been identified as DGA

EPA-UH-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First execution of critical windows command on this host: {default|featureValue|histogram} by the user
EPA-UH-F.ReasonTemplate: First execution of critical windows command {default|event.process_name} on host {asset|featureValue|histogram} by the user
EPA-UH-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time Exabeam has seen this critical windows command being executed on this host. Hosts normally execute the same processes, a first time appearance of a critical windows command is therefore notable since it may be an indicator of malicious activity.
EPA-UH-F.RuleName: First execution of critical windows command on this host by the user

EPA-UH-Pen-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First time pentest tool has been seen: {default|featureValue}.
EPA-UH-Pen-F.ReasonTemplate: First time pentest tool has been seen: {default|featureValue}.
EPA-UH-Pen-F.RuleDescription: A known pentest tool/software/program has been used/executed by the user for the first time. A first time use for a pentest tool could indicate an active attack.

EPA-UP-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal execution of process for user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-A.RuleDescription: A process has been executed by this user. Exabeam has determined that while this process has run previously, this user rarely runs it and therefore it may indicate suspicious activity.
EPA-UP-A.RuleName: Abnormal execution of process for user

EPA-UP-ALERT-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal security alert for executing this process by the user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal security alert for executing process {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-A.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that this alert has been triggered for this process in the past yet it is still considered abnormal activity. This activity may be an early indication of compromise of a user by malware or other malicious actors.
EPA-UP-ALERT-A.RuleName: Abnormal security alert for executing this process by the user

EPA-UP-ALERT-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First security alert for executing this process by the user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-F.ReasonTemplate: First security alert for executing process {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time that Exabeam has seen this user triggering an alert for this process. This activity may be an early indication of compromise of a user by malware or other malicious actors.
EPA-UP-ALERT-F.RuleName: First security alert for executing this process by the user

EPA-UP-ALERT-N.AggregateReasonTemplate: Common security alert for executing this process by the user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-N.ReasonTemplate: Common security alert for executing process {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-ALERT-N.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted that it is common for this alert to be triggered by this user when they run this process. Even though it is common, it is still worth noting when an alert is triggered.
EPA-UP-ALERT-N.RuleName: Common security alert for executing this process by the user

EPA-UP-CENUM.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of unique credential enumeration tools run by this user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-CENUM.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of unique credential enumeration tools ({quantity|featureValue}) were run by this user, expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-CENUM.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted abnormal number of unique credential enumeration tools run by this user. This is suspicious because such tools can be used in gathering information and making configuration changes to Windows systems.
EPA-UP-CENUM.RuleName: Abnormal number of unique credential enumeration tools run by this user

EPA-UP-Commands-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal execution of process for user: {default|featureValue} with the command curl/wget
EPA-UP-Commands-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal execution of process {default|featureValue} with the command curl/wget
EPA-UP-Commands-A.RuleDescription: A process with wget or curl commands has been abnormally executed by this user. This is notable because while this process has run previously, this user rarely runs it and it contains the commands wget or curl that are often used in malicious activities.
EPA-UP-Commands-A.RuleName: Abnormal process execution containing wget or curl commands for the user.

EPA-UP-Commands-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First execution of process for user: {default|featureValue} with the command curl/wget
EPA-UP-Commands-F.ReasonTemplate: First execution of process {default|featureValue} with the command curl/wget
EPA-UP-Commands-F.RuleDescription: First time this process that contains wget or curl commands has been executed by this user. This is notable because users normally run the same processes to perform their tasks, so a first time appearance of a process is notable, specifically with wget or curl commands which are often used in malicious activities.
EPA-UP-Commands-F.RuleName: First execution of this process for user and the command of the process is curl/wget

EPA-UP-CrontabMod-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal execution of crontab modification for user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-UP-CrontabMod-A.RuleDescription: A process with crontab modification commands has been abnormally executed by this user. This is notable because while this process has run previously, this user rarely runs it and may be an indicator of malicious activity.
EPA-UP-CrontabMod-A.RuleName: Abnormal execution of of process which contains commands for crontab modification for user.

EPA-UP-CrontabMod-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First execution of crontab modification for user: {default|featureValue}
EPA-UP-CrontabMod-F.RuleDescription: First time this user has run this process which contains crontab modification commands. This is notable because users normally run the same processes to perform their tasks, so a first time appearance of a process is therefore notable and may be an indicator of malicious activity.
EPA-UP-CrontabMod-F.RuleName: First execution of process which contains commands for crontab modification for user.

EPA-UP-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First execution of process for user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time Exabeam has seen this user running this process. Users normally run the same processes to perform their tasks, a first time appearance of a process is therefore notable since it may be an indicator of malicious activity
EPA-UP-F.RuleName: First execution of process for user

EPA-UP-HENUM.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of unique host enumeration tools run by this user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-HENUM.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of unique host enumeration tools ({quantity|featureValue}) were run by this user, expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
EPA-UP-HENUM.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted abnormal number of unique host enumeration tools run by this user. This is suspicious because such tools can be used in gathering information and making configuration changes to Windows systems.
EPA-UP-HENUM.RuleName: Abnormal number of unique host enumeration tools run by this user

EPA-USequenceSize-PS.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of powershell executions in the org: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-USequenceSize-PS.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of powershell executions ({quantity|featureValue}), expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
EPA-USequenceSize-PS.RuleDescription: Exabeam noticed an abnormal number of powershell executions. Users normally have a consistent activity behavior, this sequence is notable because the user performed order of magnitude more powershell executions than usual.
EPA-USequenceSize-PS.RuleName: Abnormal number of powershell executions for the user

EPA-USequenceSize-WC.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of critical windows command executions by the user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
EPA-USequenceSize-WC.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of critical windows command executions ({quantity|featureValue}), expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
EPA-USequenceSize-WC.RuleDescription: Exabeam noticed an abnormal number of critical windows command executions. These commands are typically used by malware. The commands are: tasklist,ver,ipconfig,systeminfo,net time,netstat,whoami,net start,qprocess,query,net view,net use,type,net user,net localgroup,net group,net config,net share,at,reg,wmic,wusa,netsh advfirewall,sc,rundll32
EPA-USequenceSize-WC.RuleName: Abnormal number of critical windows command executions by the user

ETW-Trace-Disable.AggregateReasonTemplate: Event tracing has been disabled, possible logging evasion
ETW-Trace-Disable.ReasonTemplate: Event tracing has been disabled, possible logging evasion
ETW-Trace-Disable.RuleDescription: The event trace log, ETW, has been disabled. This activity can aid in hiding activity. Logging evasion is notable and should be further scrutinized. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_etw_trace_evasion.yml
ETW-Trace-Disable.RuleExpression: toLower(process_name)='wevtutil.exe' && ((containsAny(toLower(command_line), ' cl ', ' clear-log') && contains(toLower(command_line), '/trace')) || (containsAny(toLower(command_line), ' sl', ' set-log') && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /e:false'))) && !WasRuleFired('ETW-Trace-Disable')
ETW-Trace-Disable.RuleName: Event tracing has been disabled, possible logging evasion

EXPERT-PENTEST-DOMAINS.RuleDescription: Exabeam has identified a domain name used by hacking tools such as Mimikatz and Kekeo in Pass-the-Hash/Golden-Ticket credential attacks. These attacks involve stealing the cached credentials left by a user on a computer or forging Kerberos authentication tickets

EXPERT-POWERSHELL-ENCRYPTED.AggregateReasonTemplate: Encrypted argument in a Powershell command detected: {default|featureValue}
EXPERT-POWERSHELL-ENCRYPTED.ReasonTemplate: Encrypted argument in a Powershell command detected
EXPERT-POWERSHELL-ENCRYPTED.RuleDescription: This behavior may indicate an attempt to bypass detection with malicious activity such as exfiltration software or payloads.
EXPERT-POWERSHELL-ENCRYPTED.RuleName: Encrypted argument in a Powershell command detected

EliseBackdoor.AggregateReasonTemplate: Backdoor activity, artifacts seen by Elise APT
EliseBackdoor.ReasonTemplate: Backdoor activity, artifacts seen by Elise APT
EliseBackdoor.RuleDescription: Activity that can allow a backdoor compromise to occur was observed. Specifically, artifacts from Elise APT were seen. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_elise.yml
EliseBackdoor.RuleName: Possible backdooring activity as seen by Elise APT

Emotet.AggregateReasonTemplate: Artifacts of Emotet malware have been observed
Emotet.ReasonTemplate: Artifacts of Emotet malware have been observed
Emotet.RuleDescription: A process associated with the Emotet malware has been executed. Command line parameters containing strings associated with this malware were observed. Emotet is used as dropper malware, potentially introducing other unwanted malware. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_emotet.yml
Emotet.RuleName: A process associated with the Emotet malware has been executed

Empire-Monkey.RuleDescription: EmpireMonkey APT activity was found. This is notable because it is a command-line execution likely through Powershell used to discover information or execute code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_empiremonkey.yml

EquationEditor-Droppers.AggregateReasonTemplate: Equation Editor: 'eqnetd32.exe', a known vulnerable exe, has been run
EquationEditor-Droppers.ReasonTemplate: Equation Editor: 'eqnetd32.exe', a known vulnerable exe, has been run
EquationEditor-Droppers.RuleDescription: EquationEditor was used. This is a known built in tool used by attackers due to its ability for exploitation. This activity is seen in CVE-2017-11882. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_exploit_cve_2017_11882.yml

EventLog-Tamper.AggregateReasonTemplate: Event log has been tampered with
EventLog-Tamper.ReasonTemplate: Event log has been tampered with
EventLog-Tamper.RuleDescription: The event log has been accessed in some form, possibly clearing the log or modification to the logging configuration. This hide an attacker's activity. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_eventlog_clear.yml
EventLog-Tamper.RuleExpression: ((toLower(process_name)='wevtutil.exe' && containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'clear-log', ' cl ', 'set-log', ' sl ')) || (toLower(process_name)='powershell.exe' && containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'clear-eventLog', 'remove-eventLog', 'limit-eventlog')) || (toLower(process_name)='wmic.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' cleareventlog '))) && !WasRuleFired('EventLog-Tamper')

Exec-Outlook-Temp.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious program was executed in the Outlook temp folder.
Exec-Outlook-Temp.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious program was executed in the Outlook temp folder.
Exec-Outlook-Temp.RuleDescription: A suspicious program was executed in the Outlook temp folder. This is notable because this could be a sign of a malicious attachment used to gain access to the user's system or sensitive information. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_outlook_temp.yml
Exec-Outlook-Temp.RuleName: A suspicious program was executed in the Outlook temp folder.

Executable-Suspicious-Folder.RuleDescription: Software and executables normally run from known specific folders, while other folders generally do not contain executables and thus should not have programs execute directly from those paths. Software running outside of known paths can indicate malicious software. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_exec_folder.yml
Executable-Suspicious-Folder.RuleName: A process has been run from a binary located in a suspicious folder

Exfil-Tunnel-Tools-Exec.RuleName: Tools known for data exfiltration and tunneling were executed.

FAIL-PTH-ALERT-dH.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible unsuccessful pass the hash attack by the user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-dH.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious failed NTLM Logon to unrecognized asset {default|event.dest_host}. Possible pass-the-hash attack
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-dH.RuleCategory: Pass The Hash and Golden Ticket
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-dH.RuleDescription: It is possible that a pass the hash attack is attempted with this user account, but the attempt failed. Even though the attempt failed, this is still significant because it may indicate a compromised host or account. A PtH attack exploits a vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication process by providing a password hash, and not the actual password to gain access to a host.
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-dH.RuleName: Possible unsuccessful pass the hash attack by the user

FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible unsuccessful pass the hash attack from the source: {default|featureValue|histogram}
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious failed NTLM Logon from {asset.server|event.src_ip|info} to unrecognized asset {default|featureValue}. Possible failed pass-the-hash attack
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleCategory: Pass The Hash and Golden Ticket
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleDescription: It is possible that a pass the hash attack is attempted from this source, but the attempt failed. Even though the attempt failed, this is still significant because it may indicate a compromised host or account. A PtH attack exploits a vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication process by providing a password hash, and not the actual password to gain access to a host.
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleExpression: length(src_host_windows)=16 && !(containsAny(src_host_windows, '_', '-')) && num_observations=0 && count(src_host_windows, 'failed-logon')=1 && isRandomHostname(src_host_windows) && auth_package='ntlm' && InList(event_code, '4625','529','530','531','532','533','534','535','539')
FAIL-PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleName: Possible unsuccessful pass the hash attack from the source

Firewall-Disabled-Netsh.AggregateReasonTemplate: Windows firewall was disabled using netsh commands.
Firewall-Disabled-Netsh.ReasonTemplate: Windows firewall was disabled using netsh commands.
Firewall-Disabled-Netsh.RuleDescription: Windows firewall was turned off using netsh commands. This could be a legitimate administrator action but is still notable as it could be used for defense evasion. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_firewall_disable.yml
Firewall-Disabled-Netsh.RuleExpression: event_code='4688' && containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'netsh firewall set opmode mode=disable') || contains(toLower(command_line), 'netsh advfirewall set') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'state off') && !WasRuleFired('Firewall-Disabled-Netsh')
Firewall-Disabled-Netsh.RuleName: Windows firewall was turned off using netsh commands.

Formbook.AggregateReasonTemplate: Process execution with patterns similar to Formbook where code is injected into a set of files in the System32 folder with commands to delete dropper from AppData Temp folder.
Formbook.ReasonTemplate: Process execution with patterns similar to Formbook where code is injected into a set of files in the System32 folder with commands to delete dropper from AppData Temp folder.
Formbook.RuleDescription: Process execution used by Formbook where code is injected into a set of files in the System32 folder was executed  with commands to delete dropper from AppData Temp folder. This is notable as it could indicate possible Formbook usage which has capabilities such as stealing passwords, keylogging, taking screenshots, and browsing files while avoiding detection. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_formbook.yml
Formbook.RuleExpression: event_code=1 && ((contains(toLower(parent_command_line), 'c:\\windows\\system32\\') && contains(toLower(parent_command_line), '.exe')) || (contains(toLower(parent_command_line), 'c:\\windows\\syswow64\\') && contains(toLower(parent_command_line), '.exe'))) && ((contains(command_line, ' /c del "c:\\users\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\appdata\\local\\temp\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '.exe')) || (contains(command_line, ' /c del "c:\\users\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\desktop\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '.exe'))  || (contains(command_line, ' /c type nul > "c:\\users\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\desktop\\') && contains(toLower(command_line), '.exe'))) && !WasRuleFired('Formbook')

Fsutil-Sus-Invocation.RuleDescription: Suspicious parameters of fsutil such as deleting USN journal, configuring it with small size, etc., seen by NotPetya and others were found. These may be used by ransomware during an attack. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_fsutil_usage.yml
Fsutil-Sus-Invocation.RuleName: Suspicious parameters of fsutil were detected.

KL-Tf-fail.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed logon due to a malformed authentication ticket: {default|featureValue}
KL-Tf-fail.ReasonTemplate: Possible Golden ticket attack, failed logon due to a malformed authentication ticket
KL-Tf-fail.RuleDescription: This means that the user's logon attempt failed because the authentication ticket could not be decrypted. This could be indicative of a Golden Ticket attack. This could also be an indication that the Kerberos ticket was tampered with, and could be evidence of an attacker elevating their privileges.

KL-TfG.RuleDescription: This is a rare failure code for a kerberos ticket, and only occurs when the integrity check on a ticket fails. This can be indicative of highly malicious activity. This event may be related to Golden Ticket attack, and should be further investigated.

MSTSC-RDP-Hijack.RuleDescription: MSTSC is a built in Windows program used to connect to RDP clients. A suspicious command line argument that indicates the 'shadowing' of an existing RDP session was observed by Exabeam. This allows a user to view all that is going on within another user's RDP session, making this event notable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_rdp_hijack_shadowing.yml
MSTSC-RDP-Hijack.RuleName: MSTSC Shadowing, possible RDP session hijack/shadowing of session

NSniff-Cred.RuleDescription: Potential network sniffing was observed. Network sniffing refers to using the network interface on a system to monitor or capture information sent over a wired or wireless connection. An adversary may place a network interface into promiscuous mode to passively access data in transit over the network, or use span ports to capture a larger amount of data. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_network_sniffing.yml

NTLM-mismatch.AggregateReasonTemplate: Mismatch between logged hostname {default|featureValue} and resolved hostname {asset|event.src_host} in NTLM authentication
NTLM-mismatch.ReasonTemplate: Mismatch between logged hostname {default|featureValue} and resolved hostname {asset|event.src_host} in NTLM authentication
NTLM-mismatch.RuleDescription: Exabeam has found a mismatch between a previously unseen hostname in a new event and the hostname resolved based on the IP address in the event. In NTLM authentication the logged hostname can be spoofed, however the IP is real. The mismatch could indicate a Pass the Hash attack originating from the host.
NTLM-mismatch.RuleExpression: ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual() && num_observations=0 && exists(src_host) && exists(ntlm_host) && count(ntlm_host, 'remote-access','remote-logon')=1 && toLower(src_host)!=toLower(ntlm_host)
NTLM-mismatch.RuleName: Mismatch between logged and resolved hostnames for host

Non-Interactive-Powershell.RuleDescription: Non-Interactive Powershell activity was found with powershell.exe process without parent process of 'explorer.exe'. NotPetya-Activity.RuleDescription: Artifacts of ransomware, NotPetya, were observed. Specifically, extracted passwords are passed back to the main module via named pipe, the file system journal of drive C is deleted and windows eventlogs are cleared using wevtutil. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_notpetya.yml
NotPetya-Activity.RuleExpression: (toLower(process_name)='fsutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' deletejournal ')) || ((contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\\\.\\pipe\\')) || (toLower(process_name)='wevtutil.exe' && contains(toLower(command_line), ' cl ')) || (toLower(process_name)='rundll32.exe' && endswith(toLower(command_line), '.dat,#1'))) && !WasRuleFired('NotPetya-Activity')

OpenWith-Exec-Cmd.RuleDescription: Command line parameters to execute OpenWith.exe were observed. OpenWith.exe is a living-off-the-land software (LOLbins), highly useful for attackers, making this event suspicious. This can also be a legitimate use of OpenWith.exe by a legitimate user, but is still notable as command line is an uncommon way to execute OpenWith.exe. Operation-Wocao-Activity.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible Operation-Wocao APT activity, suspicious command line arguments
Operation-Wocao-Activity.ReasonTemplate: Possible Operation-Wocao APT activity, suspicious command line arguments
Operation-Wocao-Activity.RuleDescription: Operation-Wocao is a known threat group. Command line parameters that could indicate enumeration were observed. This activity can lead to more serious activity such as lateral movement. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_wocao.yml
Operation-Wocao-Activity.RuleExpression: (containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'checkadmin.exe 127.0.0.1 -all', 'netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name=powershell dir=in', 'cmd /c powershell.exe -ep bypass -file c:\\s.ps1', '/tn win32times /f', 'create win32times binpath=', '\\c$\\windows\\system32\\devmgr.dll', ' -exec bypass -enc jgag', 'iie.exe iie.txt') || (contains(toLower(command_line),'type ') && contains(toLower(command_line),'keepass\\keepass.config.xml')) || (contains(toLower(command_line), 'reg query hkey_current_user\\software\\') && contains(toLower(command_line),'\\putty\\sessions\\'))) && !WasRuleFired('Operation-Wocao-Activity')
Operation-Wocao-Activity.RuleName: Possible Operation-Wocao APT activity, suspicious command line arguments

PTH-ALERT-sH.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible pass the hash attack from the source: {default|featureValue|histogram}
PTH-ALERT-sH.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious NTLM Logon from {asset.server|event.src_ip|info} to unrecognized asset {default|featureValue}. Possible pass-the-hash attack
PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleCategory: Pass The Hash and Golden Ticket
PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleDescription: It is possible that a pass the hash attack is attempted from this source. A PtH attack exploits a vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication process by providing a password hash, and not the actual password to gain access to a host.
PTH-ALERT-sH.RuleName: Possible pass the hash attack from the source

PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed pass the hash attack from the source: {default|featureValue}
PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious NTLM Logon from {asset.server|event.src_ip|info} to unrecognized asset {default|featureValue}. Possible pass-the-hash attack
PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.RuleCategory: Pass The Hash and Golden Ticket
PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.RuleDescription: It is possible that a pass the hash attack is attempted from this source. A PtH attack exploits a vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication process by providing a password hash, and not the actual password to gain access to a host.
PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.RuleExpression: contains(toLower(auth_process), 'ntlmssp') and  !contains(toLower(user), 'anonymous') and contains(toLower(logon_type), '3') and contains(toLower(auth_package), 'ntlm') and contains(toLower(key_length), '0') and contains(toLower(subject_sid), 'null sid') and containsAny(toLower(result_code), '0xc000006a' , '0xc0000064') and !WasRuleFired('PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed')
PTH-ALERT-sH-Failed.RuleName: Failed pass the hash attack with keylength of 0 in NTLM event and a 'null' sid.

PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible pass the hash attack from the source: {default|featureValue}
PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious NTLM Logon from {asset.server|event.src_ip|info} to unrecognized asset {default|featureValue}. Possible pass-the-hash attack
PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.RuleCategory: Pass The Hash and Golden Ticket
PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.RuleDescription: It is possible that a pass the hash attack is attempted from this source. A PtH attack exploits a vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication process by providing a password hash, and not the actual password to gain access to a host.
PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.RuleExpression: contains(toLower(auth_process), 'ntlmssp') and  !contains(toLower(user), 'anonymous') and contains(toLower(logon_type), '3') and contains(toLower(auth_package), 'ntlm') and contains(toLower(key_length), '0') and contains(toLower(subject_sid), 'null sid') and !WasRuleFired('PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible')
PTH-ALERT-sH-Possible.RuleName: Possible pass the hash attack with keylength of 0 in NTLM event and a 'null' sid.

Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible privilege escalation using weak service permissions
Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms.ReasonTemplate: Possible privilege escalation using weak service permissions
Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms.RuleDescription: Sc.exe, the application used to interact with Windows services, was observed changing a service ImagePath/FailureCommand. When paths used by services change, this could allow escalation of privileges and allow code to run with elevated permissions. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_using_sc_to_change_sevice_image_path_by_non_admin.yml
Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms.RuleExpression: event_code='1' and toLower(process_name)='sc.exe' and toLower(integrity)='medium' and ((contains(toLower(command_line), 'config') && contains(toLower(command_line),'binpath')) or (contains(toLower(command_line), 'failure') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'command'))) && !WasRuleFired('Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms')
Possible-PrivEsc-SvcPerms.RuleName: Possible privilege escalation using weak service permissions

Powershell-Advanced-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal user,{default|featureValue|histogram}, performing advanced powershell capabilities

Powershell-Commands-F.RuleDescription: First time this user has used this Powershell command

Powershell-Empire.RuleDescription: Powershell Empire is a tool purposefully used by attackers to perform malicious activity leveraging powershell. Powershell-Empire.RuleName: The attacker tool, Powershell Empire, has been used

Powershell-Exec-DLL.RuleName: PowerShell Strings applied to rundllas.exe seen in PowerShdll.dll

RLA-UsZ-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal communication from network zone {default|featureValue|histogram} for the user

RLA-dZsZ-A.RuleExpression: HasValue('zone_info', src) && HasValue('zone_info', dest) && GetValue('zone_info',dest)!=GetValue('zone_info',src) && num_observations>0 && num_observations<percentile_threshold_count && ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual()

RLA-dZsZ-F.RuleName: First inter-zone communication from destination to source

RLA-sZdZ-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal communication from network zone {location.zone|scopeValue|histogram} to network zone {location.zone|featureValue} for the organization
RLA-sZdZ-A.RuleExpression: HasValue('zone_info', src) && HasValue('zone_info', dest) && GetValue('zone_info',dest)!=GetValue('zone_info',src) && num_observations>0 && num_observations<percentile_threshold_count && ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual()

RLA-sZdZ-F.ReasonTemplate: First communication from network zone {location.zone|scopeValue|histogram} to network zone {location.zone|featureValue} for the organization
RLA-sZdZ-F.RuleDescription: First time a communication between these zones is observed
RLA-sZdZ-F.RuleExpression: HasValue('zone_info', src) && HasValue('zone_info', dest) && GetValue('zone_info',dest)!=GetValue('zone_info',src) && num_observations=0 && ConfidenceFactorAboveOrEqual()
RLA-sZdZ-F.RuleName: First inter-zone communication from source to destination

Regsvr32-Suspicious-Cmd.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious command line arguments related to regsvr32.exe have been observed.
Regsvr32-Suspicious-Cmd.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious command line arguments related to regsvr32.exe have been observed.
Regsvr32-Suspicious-Cmd.RuleDescription: Regsvr32.exe can be used to modify DLLs. Suspicious command line arguments related to regsvr32.exe were detected. This is notable as these commands may be part of a script to bypass application whitelisting.  Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_regsvr32_anomalies.yml
Regsvr32-Suspicious-Cmd.RuleName: Suspicious commands related to regscr32.exe have been observed.

Remote-Powershell-Session.AggregateReasonTemplate: Remote Powershell session was detected by monitoring for wsmprovhost as a parent or child process.
Remote-Powershell-Session.ReasonTemplate: Remote Powershell session was detected by monitoring for wsmprovhost as a parent or child process.
Remote-Powershell-Session.RuleDescription: Remote Powershell session was detected by monitoring for wsmprovhost as a parent or child process which are signs of an active Powershell remote session. This can be a legitimate usage of remote Powershell for monitoring purposes but should still be noted. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_remote_powershell_session_process.yml
Remote-Powershell-Session.RuleName: Remote Powershell session was detected by monitoring for wsmprovhost as a parent or child process.

Rubeus-CMD-Tool.AggregateReasonTemplate: Command line parameters: {default|featureValue} used by Rubeus hack tool detected
Rubeus-CMD-Tool.ReasonTemplate: Command line parameters: {default|featureValue} used by Rubeus hack tool detected
Rubeus-CMD-Tool.RuleDescription: Command line parameters used by the attacker tool, Rubeus, were observed. This tool is used to manipulate components of Kerberos at the traffic and host levels. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_hack_rubeus.yml
Rubeus-CMD-Tool.RuleExpression: containsAny(toLower(command_line), ' asreproast ', ' dump //service:krbtgt ', ' kerberoast ', ' createnetonly //program:', ' ptt //ticket:', ' //impersonateuser:', ' renew //ticket:', ' asktgt //user:', ' harvest //interval:') && !WasRuleFired('Rubeus-CMD-Tool')
Rubeus-CMD-Tool.RuleName: Command line parameters used by Rubeus hack tool detected

RunDll32-ControlPanel.AggregateReasonTemplate: RunDll32 executed by control panel, possible code execution attempt
RunDll32-ControlPanel.ReasonTemplate: RunDll32 executed by control panel, possible code execution attempt
RunDll32-ControlPanel.RuleDescription: Control.exe, the control panel, has spawned 'rundll32.exe', a binary used by attackers to run malicious code. This is a known tactic used by the Equation Group. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_control_dll_load.yml

SA-AsU-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal access of admin share {default|event.admin_share_name} in {default|event.dest_host}
SA-AsU-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal access of admin share {default|event.admin_share_name} in {default|event.dest_host}
SA-AsU-A.RuleDescription: This is a share access event in which user is accessing an admin share. This event is notable because it is abnormal for this user to accessed this admin share which may be an indication for lateral movement.

SA-AsU-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First access of admin share {default|event.admin_share_name} in {default|event.dest_host}
SA-AsU-F.ReasonTemplate: First access of admin share {default|event.admin_share_name} in {default|event.dest_host}
SA-AsU-F.RuleDescription: This is a share access event in which user is accessing an admin share. This event is notable because it is the first time this user has accessed this admin share which may be an indication for lateral movement.

SA-Bloodhound.AggregateReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share lsarpc folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound.ReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share lsarpc folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted lsarpc folder accessed through admin IPC share on this asset. This event is normal behavior but would be notable when it occurs with other IPC admin share access
SA-Bloodhound.RuleExpression: contains(event_code, '5145') and endsWith(toLower(file_path), 'lsarpc') and contains(toLower(share_name), 'ipc$') and exists(src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound',src_port)
SA-Bloodhound.RuleName: ADMIN IPC Share lsarpc folder accessed

SA-Bloodhound-2.AggregateReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share samr folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound-2.ReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share samr folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound-2.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted samr folder accessed through admin IPC share on this asset. This event is normal behavior but would be notable when it occurs with other IPC admin share access
SA-Bloodhound-2.RuleExpression: contains(event_code, '5145') and endsWith(toLower(file_path), 'samr') and contains(toLower(share_name), 'ipc$') and exists(src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-2',src_port)
SA-Bloodhound-2.RuleName: ADMIN IPC Share samr folder accessed

SA-Bloodhound-3.AggregateReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share srcsvc folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound-3.ReasonTemplate: ADMIN IPC Share srcsvc folder accessed by this user
SA-Bloodhound-3.RuleDescription: Exabeam noted srcsvc folder accessed through admin IPC share on this asset. This event is normal behavior but would be notable when it occurs with other IPC admin share access
SA-Bloodhound-3.RuleExpression: contains(event_code, '5145') and endsWith(toLower(file_path), 'srvsvc')  and contains(toLower(share_name), 'ipc$') and exists(src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-3',src_port)

SA-Bloodhound-Main.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user
SA-Bloodhound-Main.ReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user
SA-Bloodhound-Main.RuleDescription: Numerous share destinations on the admin IPC share were accessed by the user, which is normally only done by the Bloodhound/Sharphound attack tool. IPC Share access alone is not harmful, though the specific file paths accessed on the IPC admin share are normally only seen by the Bloodhound network windows domain enumeration tool. Using this tool can provide valuable information to both IT Admins, and especially attackers, highlighting the best possible path to attack.
SA-Bloodhound-Main.RuleName: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user

SA-Bloodhound-Main-1.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing srcsvc folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-1.ReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing srcsvc folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-1.RuleDescription: Numerous share destinations on the admin IPC share were accessed by the user, which is normally only done by the Bloodhound/Sharphound attack tool. IPC Share access alone is not harmful, though the specific file paths accessed on the IPC admin share are normally only seen by the Bloodhound network windows domain enumeration tool. Using this tool can provide valuable information to both IT Admins, and especially attackers, highlighting the best possible path to attack.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-1.RuleExpression: HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound', src_port) && HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-2', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-2', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-3', src_port)
SA-Bloodhound-Main-1.RuleName: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing srcsvc folder.

SA-Bloodhound-Main-2.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing lsarpc folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-2.ReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing lsarpc folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-2.RuleDescription: Numerous share destinations on the admin IPC share were accessed by the user, which is normally only done by the Bloodhound/Sharphound attack tool. IPC Share access alone is not harmful, though the specific file paths accessed on the IPC admin share are normally only seen by the Bloodhound network windows domain enumeration tool. Using this tool can provide valuable information to both IT Admins, and especially attackers, highlighting the best possible path to attack.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-2.RuleExpression: HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-2', src_port) && HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-3', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-1', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-3', src_port)
SA-Bloodhound-Main-2.RuleName: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing lsarpc folder.

SA-Bloodhound-Main-3.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing samr folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-3.ReasonTemplate: Possible Bloodhound Tool Usage by this user accessing samr folder.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-3.RuleDescription: Numerous share destinations on the admin IPC share were accessed by the user, which is normally only done by the Bloodhound/Sharphound attack tool. IPC Share access alone is not harmful, though the specific file paths accessed on the IPC admin share are normally only seen by the Bloodhound network windows domain enumeration tool. Using this tool can provide valuable information to both IT Admins, and especially attackers, highlighting the best possible path to attack.
SA-Bloodhound-Main-3.RuleExpression: HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound', src_port) && HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-3', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-2', src_port) && !HasRuleTriggered('SA-Bloodhound-Main-1', src_port)

SEQ-UH-01.AggregateReasonTemplate: Account lockout on an asset that belongs to this user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-01.ReasonTemplate: Account lockout on asset {asset|featureValue|histogram} that belongs to this user
SEQ-UH-01.RuleDescription: Exabeam determines whether an asset belongs to a user based on Exabeam's workstation model. This is a risk reducing event because it is less risky for users to fail logons to their own machines.
SEQ-UH-01.RuleName: Account lockout on an asset that belongs to this user

SEQ-UH-02.AggregateReasonTemplate: Account lockout on an asset that does not belong to this user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-02.ReasonTemplate: Account lockout on an asset {asset|featureValue|histogram} that does not belong to this user
SEQ-UH-02.RuleDescription: Exabeam determines whether an asset belongs to a user based on Exabeam's workstation model. This is a risk increasing event because it is more risky for users to fail logons to machine's that do not belong to them.
SEQ-UH-02.RuleName: Account lockout on an asset that does not belong to this user

SEQ-UH-03.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed logon to a top failed logon asset by user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-03.ReasonTemplate: Failed logon to a top failed logon asset {asset|featureValue|histogram} by user
SEQ-UH-03.RuleDescription: A top failed logon asset is a machine for which failed logons are common. This is a risk reducing event because failed logons happen relatively often on this machine.
SEQ-UH-03.RuleName: Failed logon to a top failed logon asset by user

SEQ-UH-04.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed logon by a service account: {default|featureValue}
SEQ-UH-04.ReasonTemplate: Failed logon by a service account
SEQ-UH-04.RuleDescription: A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. This is risk reducing event because it is more common for service accounts to fail logons.
SEQ-UH-04.RuleName: Failed logon by a service account

SEQ-UH-05.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed interactive logon by a service account: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-05.ClassifyIf: InList(event_code,'4625','529','530','531','532','533','534','535','539') and not InList(user,'local service','network service','system') and InList(logon_type,'2','7','9','10','11')
SEQ-UH-05.ReasonTemplate: Failed interactive logon by a service account {user|event.user|histogram}
SEQ-UH-05.RuleDescription: A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. This is a risk increasing event because it is less likely that a service account will fail to logon.
SEQ-UH-05.RuleName: Failed interactive logon by a service account

SEQ-UH-06.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal failed logon to asset by user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-06.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal failed logon to asset {asset.workstation|event.dest_host|info} by user
SEQ-UH-06.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for this user to fail to logon to this asset. This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.
SEQ-UH-06.RuleName: Abnormal failed logon to asset by user

SEQ-UH-07.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed logon to an asset that user has not previously accessed: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SEQ-UH-07.ReasonTemplate: Failed logon to an asset {asset|featureValue|histogram} that this user has not previously accessed
SEQ-UH-07.RuleDescription: This is the first time this user has attempted to log on to this asset. This is a risk increasing event because it is worth noting when a user does something that they have never done before.
SEQ-UH-07.RuleName: Failed logon to an asset that user has not previously accessed

SEQ-UH-08.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of failed logons for this user: {quantity|featureValue}

SEQ-UH-09.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal time of the week for a failed logon for user: {default|featureValue|histogram}

SEQ-UH-09.RuleDescription: It is unusual for this user to fail a logon at this time of the week. This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.

SEQ-UH-10.RuleDescription: This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.

SEQ-UH-11.RuleDescription: Changes were recently made to this account - these could be a password reset or change, an account disabled or deleted. This is a risk reducing event because these recent changes could account for a failed logon or lockout.

SEQ-UH-12.AggregateReasonTemplate: Logon attempt on a disabled account: {default|featureValue}
SEQ-UH-12.ReasonTemplate: Logon attempt on a disabled account
SEQ-UH-12.RuleDescription: This user account has been disabled but a logon attempt was made. This is a risk increasing event because disabled accounts should not be accessed.

SEQ-UH-14.AggregateReasonTemplate: Failed logon due to bad credentials: {default|featureValue}
SEQ-UH-14.ReasonTemplate: Failed logon due to bad credentials

SEQ-UH-14.RuleName: Failed logon due to bad credentials

SEQ-UH-15.RuleDescription: This user failed to login through VPN

SEQ-UH-16.RuleDescription: This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.

SEQ-UH-16-L.RuleDescription: This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.
SEQ-UH-16-L.RuleName: Exceeded number of failed logons for the user (L)

SEQ-UH-16-M.RuleDescription: This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.
SEQ-UH-16-M.RuleName: Exceeded number of failed logons for the user (M)

SEQ-UH-16-S.RuleDescription: This is a risk increasing event because unusual failed logons can be an indication that credentials may have been compromised.
SEQ-UH-16-S.RuleName: Exceeded number of failed logons for the user (S)

SEQ-UH-17.AggregateReasonTemplate: User failed logging on to at least 3 different hosts
SEQ-UH-17.ReasonTemplate: User failed logging on to at least 3 different hosts.
SEQ-UH-17.RuleDescription: The user failed to logon to 3 different hosts. This can be indicative of lateral movement or compromised credentials.
SEQ-UH-17.RuleName: User failed logging on to at least 3 different hosts

SEQ-UH-18.AggregateReasonTemplate: User failed to logon three times within 10 seconds
SEQ-UH-18.ReasonTemplate: User failed to logon three times within 10 seconds.
SEQ-UH-18.RuleDescription: The user failed to logon at least 3 times within 10 seconds. This can be indicative of lateral movement or compromised credentials.
SEQ-UH-18.RuleName: User failed to logon three times within 10 seconds

SERVICE-ACCOUNT.AggregateReasonTemplate: INTERNAL: User is a service account
SERVICE-ACCOUNT.RuleName: INTERNAL: User is a service account

SETUPCOMPLETE-PRIV-ESC.RuleDescription: SetupComplete.cmd and ParterSetupComplete.cmd objects were observed being used in a way that could indicate privilege escalation. These artifacts are referenced in CVE-2019-1378. This type of activity is notable and should be further investigated. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_exploit_cve_2019_1378.yml
SETUPCOMPLETE-PRIV-ESC.RuleName: Privilege escalation attempt using the SetupComplete.cmd object

SIGRed.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious child process {default|event.process_name} spawned from the Windows DNS service
SIGRed.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious child process {default|event.process_name} spawned from the Windows DNS service
SIGRed.RuleDescription: Exabeam detected a suspicious child process being spun off windows DNS service. This activity is known to be associated with the 'SIGred' attack against the Windows domain dns service, allowing attackers to achieve remote code execution.

SL-UA-F-VPN.AggregateReasonTemplate: First VPN connection for service account: {default|featureValue}
SL-UA-F-VPN.ReasonTemplate: First VPN connection for service account {user|event.user}
SL-UA-F-VPN.RuleDescription: A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. It is worth noting when user accounts make a new connection for the first time.
SL-UA-F-VPN.RuleName: First VPN connection for service account

SL-UH-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal access from asset for a service account: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SL-UH-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal access from asset {asset.server|event.src|info} for a service account
SL-UH-A.RuleDescription: A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. This event is notable because service accounts do not typically make contact from this server.
SL-UH-A.RuleName: Abnormal access from asset for a service account

SL-UH-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First access from asset for a service account: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SL-UH-F.ReasonTemplate: First access from asset {asset.server|event.src|info} for a service account
SL-UH-F.RuleDescription: A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. This event is notable because service accounts do not typically make contact from this server.
SL-UH-F.RuleName: First access from asset for a service account

SL-UH-I.AggregateReasonTemplate: Interactive logon using a service account: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SL-UH-I.ReasonTemplate: Interactive logon using a service account {user|event.user|histogram}
SL-UH-I.RuleDescription: An interactive logon means that the user is logging on with a domain account through Active Directory. A service account is a user account that belongs to an application rather than an end user and runs a particular piece of software. This event is notable because a service account is used by an application and not to log into an asset.
SL-UH-I.RuleName: Interactive logon using a service account

SL-sHU.AggregateReasonTemplate: INTERNAL: Sufficient access/logon data from asset: {default|featureValue|histogram}
SL-sHU.RuleName: INTERNAL: Sufficient access/logon data from asset

SW-UC.AggregateReasonTemplate: SolarWinds tool launched an unusual child process {default|featureValue}
SW-UC.ReasonTemplate: SolarWinds tool {default|event.parent_process_name} ran an unusual child process {default|event.process_name}
SW-UC.RuleDescription: An unusual Solarwinds child processes was loaded. This is notable because this child process when loaded by SolarWinds is uncommon.
SW-UC.RuleName: Unusual child process loaded by SolarWinds tool

SecX-Tool-Exec.RuleDescription: Artifacts from attacked tool, SecurityXploded, were seen. SecurityXploded Tools is used for password and credential dumps. This could warrant further investigation. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_hack_secutyxploded.yml

ServicePath-Modification.RuleDescription: The execution path used by a Windows service was modified to point to powershell or cmd.exe. This event is notable because a service running with powershell or cmd.exe can run untrusted code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_service_path_modification.yml

ShadowCP-OSUtilities.AggregateReasonTemplate: A Shadow Copy was created using operating systems utilities, possible credential theft.
ShadowCP-OSUtilities.ReasonTemplate: A Shadow Copy was created using operating systems utilities, possible credential theft.
ShadowCP-OSUtilities.RuleDescription: A Shadow Copy was created using operating systems utilities, possible credential theft. This process can be considered normal behavior but it is still notable to track such activity. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_shadow_copies_creation.yml
ShadowCP-OSUtilities.RuleName: Shadow Copies Creation Using Operating Systems Utilities

ShadowCP-SymLink.AggregateReasonTemplate: A Shadow Copy was symbolically linked using operation systems utilities.
ShadowCP-SymLink.ReasonTemplate: A Shadow Copy was symbolically linked using operation systems utilities.
ShadowCP-SymLink.RuleDescription: A Shadow Copy was symbolically linked using operation systems utilities. This action can be used to escalate privileges. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_shadow_copies_access_symlink.yml

Shim-Installation.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible installation of a 'shim' using sdbinst.exe
Shim-Installation.ReasonTemplate: Possible installation of a 'shim' using sdbinst.exe
Shim-Installation.RuleDescription: Possible installation of a shim using sdbinst.exe. This event is notable as shims can be used to intercept API calls and load malicious DLLs enabling an attacker to run malicious software. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_sdbinst_shim_persistence.yml
Shim-Installation.RuleName: Possible installation of a 'shim' using sdbinst.exe

SoundRecorder-AudioCapture.RuleDescription: The SoundRecorder has captured external audio. Alone this event is not an indicator of malicious activity, but the recording of microphone audio is itself a notable event. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_soundrec_audio_capture.yml

Squibly-Two.AggregateReasonTemplate: A WMI SquiblyTwo Attack with possibly renamed WMI by looking for imphash was detected.
Squibly-Two.ReasonTemplate: A WMI SquiblyTwo Attack with possibly renamed WMI by looking for imphash was detected.
Squibly-Two.RuleDescription: A WMI SquiblyTwo Attack with possibly renamed WMI by looking for imphash was detected. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_bypass_squiblytwo.yml
Squibly-Two.RuleName: A WMI SquiblyTwo Attack with possibly renamed WMI by looking for imphash was detected.

Sus-Double-Extension.AggregateReasonTemplate: Process executed using .exe extension after a non-executable file extension: {default|featureValue}.
Sus-Double-Extension.ReasonTemplate: Process executed using .exe extension after a non-executable file extension: {default|featureValue}.
Sus-Double-Extension.RuleDescription: Process executed using .exe extension after a non-executable file extension. This is notable as this method can hide executable files from defense mechanisms. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_double_extension.yml
Sus-Double-Extension.RuleName: An .exe extension was used after a different non-executable file extension.

Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious Powershell process was started with base64 encoded commands.
Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious Powershell process was started with base64 encoded commands.
Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine.RuleDescription: Suspicious Powershell process was started with base64 encoded commands. This is notable because Powershell can be used to discover information or execute code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_powershell_enc_cmd.yml
Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine.RuleExpression: containsAny(toLower(command_line), ' -e jab',' -e  jab',' -e   jab',' -e    jab',' -e     jab',' -e      jab',' -en jab',' -enc jab',' -enc* jab',' -w hidden -e* jab',' ba^j e-',' -e suyvi',' -e awv4i',' -e sqbfafga',' -e aqblahga',' -enc suyvi',' -enc awv4i',' -enc sqbfafga',' -enc aqblahga')  && !contains(toLower(command_line), ' -executionpolicy remotesigned ') && !WasRuleFired('Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine')
Sus-Encoded-PS-CmdLine.RuleName: Suspicious Powershell process was started with base64 encoded commands.

Sus-GUP-Usage.AggregateReasonTemplate: Execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory.
Sus-GUP-Usage.ReasonTemplate: Execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory.
Sus-GUP-Usage.RuleDescription: Execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory other than the Notepad++ updater folders. This is often used in DLL side-loading attacks. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_gup.yml
Sus-GUP-Usage.RuleName: Execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory.

Sus-MsiExec-Directory.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious msiexec process started in an uncommon directory
Sus-MsiExec-Directory.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious msiexec process started in an uncommon directory
Sus-MsiExec-Directory.RuleDescription: Suspicious msiexec process started in an uncommon directory. This could be a method to evade detection by renaming malicious files. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_msiexec_cwd.yml
Sus-MsiExec-Directory.RuleName: Suspicious msiexec process started in an uncommon directory.

Sus-Powershell-Invocation-Parent-Proc.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious Powershell invocation from interpreters or unusual programs.
Sus-Powershell-Invocation-Parent-Proc.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious Powershell invocation from interpreters or unusual programs.
Sus-Powershell-Invocation-Parent-Proc.RuleDescription: Suspicious Powershell invocation from interpreters or unusual programs. This is notable because Powershell can be used to discover information or execute code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_powershell_parent_combo.yml
Sus-Powershell-Invocation-Parent-Proc.RuleName: Suspicious Powershell invocation from interpreters or unusual programs.

Sus-Powershell-Param.AggregateReasonTemplate: Powershell was invoked with a suspicious parameter substring
Sus-Powershell-Param.ReasonTemplate: Powershell was invoked with a suspicious parameter substring
Sus-Powershell-Param.RuleDescription: Powershell was invoked with a suspicious parameter substring. This is notable because the Powershell execution argument was obfuscated, common in Powershell attack frameworks. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_powershell_suspicious_parameter_variation.yml
Sus-Powershell-Param.RuleExpression: toLower(process_name)='powershell.exe' && inList(toLower(command_line), ' -windowstyle h ',' -windowstyl h',' -windowsty h',' -windowst h',' -windows h',' -windo h',' -wind h',' -win h',' -wi h',' -win h ',' -win hi ',' -win hid ',' -win hidd ',' -win hidde ',' -nopr ',' -nopro ',' -noprof ',' -noprofi ',' -noprofil ',' -nonin ',' -nonint ',' -noninte ',' -noninter ',' -nonintera ',' -noninterac ',' -noninteract ',' -noninteracti ',' -noninteractiv ',' -ec ',' -encodedcomman ',' -encodedcomma ',' -encodedcomm ',' -encodedcom ',' -encodedco ',' -encodedc ',' -encoded ',' -encode ',    ' -encod ',' -enco ',' -en ') && !WasRuleFired('Sus-Powershell-Param')
Sus-Powershell-Param.RuleName: Powershell was invoked with a suspicious parameter substring

Sus-Procdump.AggregateReasonTemplate: Detected suspicious use of Procdump using command {default|featureValue}
Sus-Procdump.ReasonTemplate: Detected suspicious use of Procdump using command {default|featureValue}
Sus-Procdump.RuleDescription: Suspicious use of SysInternals Procdump. Special command line parameters were observed being used to access the lsass process. This can be a sign of lateral movement. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_procdump.yml

Sus-Svchost-Process.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious svchost process was started.
Sus-Svchost-Process.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious svchost process was started.
Sus-Svchost-Process.RuleDescription: A suspicious svchost process was started. This could be an attempt to manipulate features of artifacts and make them appear legitimate or benign to evade defenses and observations. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_svchost.yml
Sus-Svchost-Process.RuleName: A suspicious svchost process was started.

Suspicious-ControlPanel.AggregateReasonTemplate: Suspicious loading of a control panel item, possible code execution
Suspicious-ControlPanel.ReasonTemplate: Suspicious loading of a control panel item, possible code execution
Suspicious-ControlPanel.RuleDescription: Control panel commandlets were loaded outside of the default System32 directory. This can indicate a control panel dll was modified to allow arbitrary code execution. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_control_panel_item.yml
Suspicious-ControlPanel.RuleName: Control Panel commandlets loaded outside the default directory

Suspicious-DAT.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious .dat file used, possible APT activity
Suspicious-DAT.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious .dat file used, possible APT activity
Suspicious-DAT.RuleDescription: Artifacts from a 2018 attack against large organizations have been observed in the command line arguments. This can indicate an attack to run untruted code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_unidentified_nov_18.yml
Suspicious-DAT.RuleName: A suspicious .dat file used, possible APT activity

Suspicious-GetSystem-Usage.RuleDescription: A known artifact seen in pentester attack tools, Meterpreter and Cobalt Strike, were observed in the starting of a specific service. These are exploitation tools used by attackers. This event should be further scrutinized. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_meterpreter_or_cobaltstrike_getsystem_service_start.yml
Suspicious-GetSystem-Usage.RuleExpression: toLower(parent_process_name)='services.exe' && ((contains(toLower(command_line), 'cmd') && contains(toLower(command_line), '/c') && contains(toLower(command_line),'echo') && contains(toLower(command_line),'\\pipe\\')) || (contains(toLower(command_line), '%compsec%') && contains(toLower(command_line),'/c') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'echo') && contains(toLower(command_line), '\\pipe\\')) || (contains(toLower(command_line), 'rundll32') && contains(toLower(command_line), '.dll') && contains(toLower(command_line),'a') && contains(toLower(command_line), '/p:'))) && !contains(toLower(command_line), 'mpcmdrun') && !WasRuleFired('Suspicious-GetSystem-Usage')
Suspicious-GetSystem-Usage.RuleName: Possible Meterpeter/Cobalt Strike usage of GetSystem

Suspicious-IIS-Modules.AggregateReasonTemplate: Native-Code modules for IIS installed via command line
Suspicious-IIS-Modules.ReasonTemplate: Native-Code modules for IIS installed via command line
Suspicious-IIS-Modules.RuleDescription: Native-Code modules for IIS are not malicious themselves, but can still be abused by attackers to install backdoors on webservers. Installing via command line vs the GUI makes this event notable. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_iss_module_install.yml
Suspicious-IIS-Modules.RuleName: Native-Code modules for IIS installed via command line

Suspicious-LNK.AggregateReasonTemplate: A suspicious .dat file used, possible ATP activity
Suspicious-LNK.ReasonTemplate: A suspicious .dat file used, possible ATP activity
Suspicious-LNK.RuleDescription: Artifacts from a 2018 attack against large organizations have been observed in the command line arguments, loading of a suspicious lnk symlink. This can indicate an attack to run untruted code.
Suspicious-LNK.RuleName: A suspicious .lnk file used, possible ATP activity

Suspicious-Persistence.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible PowerSploit/Empire usage seen in 'schtasks' invocation
Suspicious-Persistence.ReasonTemplate: Possible PowerSploit/Empire usage seen in 'schtasks' invocation
Suspicious-Persistence.RuleDescription: When attacker tools, PowerSploit and Empire, are used with default configurations, 'schtask' is created, and this has been observed in powershell commands. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_powersploit_empire_schtasks.yml
Suspicious-Persistence.RuleExpression: toLower(parent_process_name)='powershell.exe' && containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'schtasks') && contains(toLower(command_line),'/create') && contains(toLower(command_line),'sc') && ((contains(toLower(command_line),'onlogon') && contains(toLower(command_line),'/tn') && contains(ToLower(command_line), 'updater') && contains(toLower(command_line), 'powershell')) || (contains(toLower(command_line),'tr') && contains(toLower(command_line),'powershell')) || (contains(toLower(command_line),'updater') && contains(toLower(command_line),'tr') && contains(toLower(command_line),'powershell')) || (contains(toLower(command_line),'tn') && contains(toLower(command_line),'tr') && contains(toLower(command_line),'powershell'))) && !WasRuleFired('Suspicious-Persistence')
Suspicious-Persistence.RuleName: Suspicious 'schtask' creation, possible attack tool usage

Suspicious-RDP-TSCON.AggregateReasonTemplate: A redirect of RDP using tscon.exe was observed
Suspicious-RDP-TSCON.ReasonTemplate: A redirect of RDP using tscon.exe was observed
Suspicious-RDP-TSCON.RuleDescription: A redirect of RDP using tscon.exe was observed. RDP is used to connect to remote windows machine. Abnormal RDP usage can indicate lateral movement. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_tscon_rdp_redirect.yml
Suspicious-RDP-TSCON.RuleName: Suspicious usage of RDP using tscon.exe

Suspicious-Shell-Child-Process.AggregateReasonTemplate: Windows shell has spawned a suspicious process
Suspicious-Shell-Child-Process.ReasonTemplate: Windows shell has spawned a suspicious process
Suspicious-Shell-Child-Process.RuleDescription: There exists a class of Windows executables that should never spawn from command line programs. When this happens, it can indicate some type of code execution attempt. Exabeam has detected a suspicious command line executable process spawning a suspicious process.
Suspicious-Shell-Child-Process.RuleName: Windows shell has spawned a suspicious process

Svchost-Suspicious-Launch.AggregateReasonTemplate: Svchost.exe has launched without any command line arguments, possible process injection
Svchost-Suspicious-Launch.ReasonTemplate: Svchost.exe has launched without any command line arguments, possible process injection
Svchost-Suspicious-Launch.RuleDescription: Svchost.exe normally spawns CLI arguments, and this event contained none. This is notable as this type of svchost activity is normally seen during process injection attacks. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_svchost_no_cli.yml
Svchost-Suspicious-Launch.RuleName: Svchost.exe has launched without any command line arguments

Sys-File-Exec-Anomaly.AggregateReasonTemplate: A Windows program executable was started in a suspicious folder.
Sys-File-Exec-Anomaly.ReasonTemplate: A Windows program executable was started in a suspicious folder.
Sys-File-Exec-Anomaly.RuleDescription: A Windows program executable was started in a suspicious folder. This could be an attempt to manipulate features of artifacts and make them appear legitimate or benign to evade defenses and observations. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_system_exe_anomaly.yml
Sys-File-Exec-Anomaly.RuleName: A Windows program executable was started in a suspicious folder.

Sysmon-Driver-Unload.RuleDescription: Command line arguments to possibly unload Sysmon driver were observed. This is notable because unloading a Sysmon driver can halt event logging to obfuscate any new processes during that time. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_sysmon_driver_unload.yml

Tap-Installer.RuleDescription: TAP software, used for VPNS, was installed. This could be a legitimate installation but is still notable for usage in data exfiltration via tunneling. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_tap_installer_execution.yml

Taskmgr-as-Parent.AggregateReasonTemplate: A process was created from Windows task manager.
Taskmgr-as-Parent.ReasonTemplate: A process was created from Windows task manager.
Taskmgr-as-Parent.RuleDescription: A process was created from Windows task manager. This could be an attempt to manipulate features of artifacts and make them appear legitimate or benign to evade defenses and observations. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_susp_taskmgr_parent.yml
Taskmgr-as-Parent.RuleName: A process was created from Windows task manager.

TasksFolder-Evasion.AggregateReasonTemplate: 'Tasks' directory seen in command line usage, possible evasion of defenses
TasksFolder-Evasion.ReasonTemplate: 'Tasks' directory seen in command line usage, possible evasion of defenses
TasksFolder-Evasion.RuleDescription: The tasks directory can be abused by attackers to allow the influencing of scripts hosts such as 'cscript' or 'regsvr32'. This can aid attackers in evading detection by security tools. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_task_folder_evasion.yml
TasksFolder-Evasion.RuleName: The 'tasks' directory was observed in a file creation command

Terminal-Svc-Proc-Spawn.AggregateReasonTemplate: A process was spawned from the terminal service server.
Terminal-Svc-Proc-Spawn.ReasonTemplate: A process was spawned from the terminal service server.
Terminal-Svc-Proc-Spawn.RuleDescription: The terminal service server, also known as Remote Desktop Services, spawned a process. This could be an indicator of the exploitation of CVE-2019-0708 where an attacker can send requests to a target system via RDP. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_termserv_proc_spawn.yml
Terminal-Svc-Proc-Spawn.RuleName: Process spawned by the terminal service server

Trickbot-Recon.AggregateReasonTemplate: Trickbot malware domain recon activity observed
Trickbot-Recon.ReasonTemplate: Trickbot malware domain recon activity observed
Trickbot-Recon.RuleDescription: Commands known to be used by Trickbot banking malware have been observed. These command attempt to enumerate domain information, useful for lateral movement attacks. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_trickbot_recon_activity.yml

TrojanLoader.AggregateReasonTemplate: Trojan Loader activity, artifacts of APT28, observed
TrojanLoader.ReasonTemplate: Trojan Loader activity, artifacts of APT28, observed
TrojanLoader.RuleDescription: Activity seen by APT28 has been observed. This includes suspicious DLL processes. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_sofacy.yml

TropicTrooper-APT.RuleDescription: The threat/attacker TropicTrooper previously targeted energy and food organizations. Artifacts of this group, namely suspicious command line arguments, were observed. Activity from this threat group can indicate lateral movement. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_tropictrooper.yml

TurlaGroup-LateralMovement.AggregateReasonTemplate: Artifacts from the ATP 'Turla Group' have been observed
TurlaGroup-LateralMovement.ReasonTemplate: Artifacts from the ATP 'Turla Group' have been observed
TurlaGroup-LateralMovement.RuleDescription: Artifacts from the ATP 'Turla Group' have been observed. These actions seen can indicate lateral movement, and should be further scrutinized. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_turla_commands.yml
TurlaGroup-LateralMovement.RuleName: Artifacts from the ATP 'Turla Group' have been observed

UA-GC-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal activity from country {location.country|featureValue|histogram} for group {user.group|scopeValue}
UA-GC-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal activity from country {location.country|featureValue|histogram} for group {user.group|scopeValue}

UserProcess-Spawned-FromOffice.ReasonTemplate: Microsoft Office application has spawned a process running under 'Users'
UserProcess-Spawned-FromOffice.RuleDescription: A Microsoft Office application has spawned a process running under the 'Users' path. This can indicate execution of malicious code. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_office_spawn_exe_from_users_directory.yml
UserProcess-Spawned-FromOffice.RuleName: An executable running under the 'Users' path has been spawned from an Office application

WEB-USequenceSize.ReasonTemplate: ({quantity|featureValue}) web activity events have been reported for {user|event.user|histogram}, expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
WEB-USequenceSize.RuleDescription: Exabeam noticed that this user had an abnormal number of web activity events. WEB-USequenceSize.RuleName: Abnormal number of web activity events for user

WEB-USequenceSize-Denied.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of denied web activity events for user

WEB-USequenceSize-Denied.RuleDescription: Exabeam noticed that this user had an abnormal number of denied web activity events. Users may violate proxy policies occasionally and get blocked. However, this day  is notable since the number of violations has been orders  of magnitude higher than usual, which may indicate a compromise or malicious behavior.
WEB-USequenceSize-Denied.RuleName: Abnormal number of denied web activity events for user

WEB-USequenceSize-JS.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of job search events by user
WEB-USequenceSize-JS.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal number of job search events ({quantity|featureValue}) for user {asset|scopeValue|histogram}, expected around {quantity|percentileThresholdValue|histogram}
WEB-USequenceSize-JS.RuleDescription: Exabeam noticed an abnormal number of job search events. Users normally have a consistent activity behavior, this sequence is notable because the user performed order of magnitude more job search than usual causing productivity loss.
WEB-USequenceSize-JS.RuleName: Abnormal number of job search events by user

WEB-UT-TOW-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal day for this user to access the web via the organization: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WEB-UT-TOW-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal day {time.time_of_week|featureValue|histogram} for {user|event.user|histogram} to access the web via the organization
WEB-UT-TOW-A.RuleDescription: It is abnormal for this user to access the web via the organization on this day of the week. This is notable because it may be an indication another user is accessing these credentials, or the user is performing rogue activities.
WEB-UT-TOW-A.RuleName: Abnormal day for this user to access the web via the organization

WEB-UU-Reputation.AggregateReasonTemplate: User attempted access to a url with bad reputation
WEB-UU-Reputation.ReasonTemplate: User attempted access to url {default|event.full_url} with bad reputation

WEB-UU-Reputation.RuleName: User attempted access to a url with bad reputation

WEB-UU-Tor.ReasonTemplate: User has accessed a URL containing '/tor/server': {default|event.full_url}

WEB-UUa-Browser-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First activity using this web browser for this user to a new domain: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WEB-UUa-Browser-F.ReasonTemplate: First activity using web browser {default|event.browser|histogram} for this user to a new domain {default|event.web_domain}
WEB-UUa-Browser-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time that Exabeam has seen this user utilizing this browser via the proxy. Users normally use a standard set of web browsers on their corporate devices. This event may indicate a rogue process such as malware.

WEB-UUa-MobileBrowser-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First activity using this mobile web browser/app for this user to a new domain: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WEB-UUa-MobileBrowser-F.ReasonTemplate: First activity using mobile web browser/app {default|event.browser|histogram} for this user to a new domain {default|event.web_domain}
WEB-UUa-MobileBrowser-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time that Exabeam has seen this user utilizing this mobile browser/app via the proxy. Since mobile devices may be owned by the users themselves (BYOD) they can usually install and run unsupervised software, however most users usually have repeating usage pattern of apps/mobile browsers, and therefor this event should be noted.
WEB-UUa-MobileBrowser-F.RuleName: First activity using this mobile web browser/app for this user to a new domain

WEB-UUa-OS-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First web activity using this operating system for this user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WEB-UUa-OS-F.ReasonTemplate: First web activity using operating system {default|event.os|histogram}
WEB-UUa-OS-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time Exabeam has seen this user utilizing this operating system via the proxy. Users normally use the same operating systems on their corporate devices. This event may indicated a rogue device or software has been used in the organization.
WEB-UUa-OS-F.RuleName: First web activity using this operating system for this user
