WEB-UZ-F.ReasonTemplate: First web activity for user {user|scopeValue|histogram} from network zone {default|featureValue}
WEB-UZ-F.RuleDescription: This is the first time that this user has attempted to access the web from this network zone. Users normally access the web from the same networks, therefor this event is notable since it may indicate a compromise.
WEB-UZ-F.RuleName: First web activity for this user in this zone

WEB-ZU.AggregateReasonTemplate: INTERNAL: Zone is not new OR it has converged for web activity: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WEB-ZU.RuleName: INTERNAL: Zone is not new OR it has converged for web activity

WINCMD-Arp.RuleDescription: User used the 'arp' program to map the ip/mac details

WINCMD-Ipconfig.AggregateReasonTemplate: Ipconfig program to check for network interfaces details was used
WINCMD-Ipconfig.ReasonTemplate: Ipconfig program to check for network interfaces details was used
WINCMD-Ipconfig.RuleDescription: User used the 'ipconfig' program to check the network interfaces

WINCMD-Netsh.RuleDescription: User used the 'netsh' program to check the firewall policies

WINCMD-Route.RuleDescription: User used the 'route' program to check for active/persistent routes

WINCMD-WmiObject.AggregateReasonTemplate: User used powershell 'get-wmiobject' to enumerate network adapter info.
WINCMD-WmiObject.ReasonTemplate: User used powershell 'get-wmiobject' to enumerate network adapter info.
WINCMD-WmiObject.RuleDescription: The powershell commandlet, 'get-wmiobject' was used to call a command module, 'win32_networkadapterconfiguration', which enumerates network adapter information.
WINCMD-WmiObject.RuleExpression: contains(event_code, '4103') and contains(toLower(command_invocation), 'get-wmiobject') and contains(toLower(command_module), 'win32_networkadapterconfiguration') and !wasRuleFired('WINCMD-WmiObject')
WINCMD-WmiObject.RuleName: Powershell WMI object to enumerate network adapter was used

WMI-Script-Event-Consumers.AggregateReasonTemplate: WMI script event consumers were found.
WMI-Script-Event-Consumers.ReasonTemplate: WMI script event consumers were found.
WMI-Script-Event-Consumers.RuleDescription: WMI script event consumers were found. This could be a legitimate usage of event consumers but is still notable as it could be an indicator of a malicious actor disabling native Windows event logging. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_wmi_persistence_script_event_consumer.yml
WMI-Script-Event-Consumers.RuleName: Suspicious usage of WMI script event consumers.

WMI-Spawn-PowerShell.RuleDescription: WMI spawned PowerShell. This could be a legitimate usage but is still notable as PowerShell being spawned via WMI is uncommon and can allow malicious actions such as downloading, creating, or overwriting executable content on the targeted system. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_wmi_spwns_powershell.yml

WMIC-EXE-RENAME-ORG-A.RuleName: Abnormal usage of WMIC.exe to rename a group by this user.

WPA-GP-A.AggregateReasonTemplate: Abnormal privileged process for peer group: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WPA-GP-A.ReasonTemplate: Abnormal privileged processes {default|featureValue} for peer group {user.group|scopeValue}
WPA-GP-A.RuleDescription: A privileged process is an external process that can be run by a non-privileged user. This is worth noting because privileged processes can be run by non-privileged users. It is abnormal for a member of this peer group to execute this privileged process.
WPA-GP-A.RuleName: Abnormal privileged process for peer group

WPA-GP-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First privileged process for peer group: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WPA-GP-F.ReasonTemplate: First privileged process {default|featureValue} for peer group {user.group|scopeValue}
WPA-GP-F.RuleDescription: A privileged process is an external process that can be run by a non-privileged user. This is worth noting because privileged processes can be run by non-privileged users. This is the first time a member of this peer group has executed a privileged process.
WPA-GP-F.RuleName: First privileged process for peer group

WPA-HP-A.RuleDescription: A privileged process is an external process that can be run by a non-privileged user. This is worth noting because privileged processes can be run by non-privileged users. This host has executed an abnormal number of privileged processes.

WPA-HP-F.RuleDescription: A privileged process is an external process that can be run by a non-privileged user. This is worth noting because privileged processes can be run by non-privileged users. This is the first time a privileged process is executed on this host.

WPA-HU.AggregateReasonTemplate: INTERNAL: Abnormal or first privileged access for user on asset: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WPA-HU.RuleName: INTERNAL: Abnormal or first privileged access for user on asset

WPA-HZ-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First privileged access event on host from zone: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WPA-HZ-F.ReasonTemplate: First privileged access from zone {asset.server|featureValue} on asset {asset|event.dest_host|histogram}
WPA-HZ-F.RuleDescription: A privileged access event is a non-privileged user gaining admin permissions. Because this grants the user greater access it is worth noting. This is the first privileged access event from this zone, on this host
WPA-HZ-F.RuleName: First privileged access event on host from zone

WPA-OG-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First privileged access event for user: {default|featureValue|histogram}
WPA-OG-F.RuleDescription: A privileged access event is a non-privileged user gaining admin permissions. Because this grants the user greater access it is worth noting. This is the first time this user has ever had a privileged access event.
WPA-OG-F.RuleName: First privileged access event for user for peer group

WPA-OH-F.AggregateReasonTemplate: First execution of critical windows command using privileged access on this host: {default|featureValue|histogram}

WannaCry.AggregateReasonTemplate: Artifacts of WannaCry ransomware have been observed
WannaCry.ReasonTemplate: Artifacts of WannaCry ransomware have been observed
WannaCry.RuleDescription: WannaCry is ransomware. Known command line artifacts or known processes were detected. This event is notable as Wannacry is a dangerous worm that can quickly spread through networks on it's own. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_malware_wannacry.yml
WannaCry.RuleExpression: (Inlist(toLower(process_name), 'tasksche.exe', 'mssecsvc.exe', 'taskdl.exe', 'taskhsvc.exe', 'taskse.exe', '111.exe', 'lhdfrgui.exe', 'linuxnew.exe', 'wannacry.exe')  || contains(toLower(process), 'wanadecryptor') || (contains(toLower(command_line),  'icacls ') && contains(toLower(command_line), ' /grant everyone:f /t /c /q')) || containsAny(toLower(command_line), 'bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no', 'wbadmin delete catalog -quiet', '@please_read_me@.txt')) && !WasRuleFired('WannaCry')
WannaCry.RuleName: Artifacts seen by WannaCry malware have been observed

WebShell-CLI.AggregateReasonTemplate: Possible command line web shell detected
WebShell-CLI.ReasonTemplate: Possible command line web shell detected
WebShell-CLI.RuleDescription: Certain commands seen during usage of a web shell were observed. These type of actions can be used during numerous stages of an attack. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_webshell_detection.yml
WebShell-CLI.RuleName: Possible command line web shell detected

WebShell-WebServer.RuleDescription: A web shell spawned from a web server has been observed. A web shell can help an attacker exfiltrate data as well as be used for C&C. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_webshell_spawn.yml
WebShell-WebServer.RuleName: Possible web server web shell detected

Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_proc_wrong_parent.yml
Win-Proc-Sus-Parent.RuleName: A suspicious parent process of well-known Windows processes was detected.

WinWord-Uncommon-Subprocess.ReasonTemplate: Winword spawned csc.exe, possible code execution

Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_exploit_cve_2017_8759.yml
WinWord-Uncommon-Subprocess.RuleName: Winword has spawned an uncommon subprocess, csc.exe

Word-FLTLDR-Exploit-Vector.AggregateReasonTemplate: CVE-2017-0261: Possible loading of exploit using Microsoft Office and the fltdr.exe application

ZxShell.RuleDescription: Artifacts of 'ZxShell', a RAT and backdooring software, have been observed. This type of software is used for CC connections. Reference: https://github.com/Neo23x0/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/win_apt_zxshell.yml
